info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description:
The public API of MonitorFlow, for scripts and integrations: a ticketing tool reading alerts, a chat bot acknowledging them, a deployment script silencing a server while it works. It is the same API the web interface uses, under `/api/v1`, with the same rules about who may see and change what.

## API keys

An administrator makes a key under **Admin › API keys**: a global administrator for anything, a customer's administrator for that customer, a site's administrator for that site. The key is shown once, when it is made: `mfk_` followed by 43 characters. MonitorFlow keeps only a hash of it, so a lost key cannot be shown again; make another one.

What a key may do is chosen when it is made and never changes. To change it, make another key and turn the first one off.

- **Access**: "Read only" (viewer, the default), "Read and change" (operator), "Approve commands" (approver) or "Administer" (administrator).
- **Reach**: everything, one customer or one site. Outside its reach, servers, sites and incidents do not exist for the key: they answer 404, and lists leave them out.
- **Areas**, all by default: `servers` (servers and relays, their metrics and logs), `alerts` (incidents, silences, on-call, follow-up, sensors, thresholds and check settings, offline alerts, notification channels), `updates` (commands, campaigns, packages, package sources, mirrors, rollback, update settings), `remediation` (AI remediation and AI commands), `dashboards`, and `administration` (everything else). A route outside the key's areas answers 403 `api_key_scope`. Any key may list servers, relays, sites and customers within its reach, to turn names into IDs. Each operation below says which area it belongs to.
- **Expiry**: 30 days, 90 days, 1 year (the default) or never.

A key acts as the person who made it, narrowed to its reach and access, checked again on every request. It never does more than its maker could at that moment: a maker who loses a role loses it for the key too, a maker who is disabled finds the key refused, and a maker who is deleted takes the key with them. The keys list shows when each key was last used, to the minute. Anyone who could have made a key can turn it off; it stops at its next request.

What a key changes is written to the audit log as its maker's action, with the key's ID, so the log tells a person from their script. The secret never appears in the audit log or the server's logs.

## Authentication

Send the key in the `Authorization` header of every request:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mfk_…" https://monitorflow.example.com/api/v1/servers
```

Keys work only under `/api/v1`; the web interface's own paths refuse them. A request with a key needs no CSRF header. A missing, malformed, unknown or expired key, or one whose maker is disabled, answers 401 `unauthenticated`.

Signing in and out, first-run setup, password and acknowledge links, display links and screens, API keys themselves, a person's own on-call contact, and inviting users or issuing their password links are not part of the public API: they answer 404 under `/api/v1`. They are for people in a browser, or they hand out a credential that would outlive the key.

## Versions and changes

`/api/v1` is a contract. Within v1, MonitorFlow only adds: new fields in answers, new optional parameters, new routes, new values of `code`. Fields are never renamed or removed and their types never change. Your client must ignore fields it does not know. When a change would break v1, MonitorFlow keeps the old shape in v1 and makes a v2 only when that becomes unreasonable.

This document is served by every central server at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, without a key.

## Conventions

- Bodies are JSON objects with `snake_case` field names. Send `Content-Type: application/json`. Bodies are at most 64 KiB; a larger one answers 413. Most routes refuse a body with a field they do not know, with 400 `invalid`.
- IDs are UUIDs. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC, like `2026-11-14T09:30:00Z`. Durations are in seconds (`_s`) or milliseconds (`_ms`), as the field name says.
- An ID that is not a UUID answers 404, like an ID that does not exist.

## Pagination

Lists that can grow without bound take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`: servers, relays, incidents, a server's commands and packages, campaigns, tokens, remediation incidents and events. Pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` to get the next page, with the same filters; it is `null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque: do not build or change them. A server or incident added between two pages neither repeats nor shifts the others. There are no page numbers or totals.

Lists that stay small (sites, customers, silences, approvals, dashboards) answer in full.

## Filters

Filters are query parameters, exact values ANDed together, like `GET /api/v1/incidents?state=open&severity=critical&site_id=…`. A bad value is 400 `invalid`, and so is an unknown parameter on the lists that say so.

## Errors

Every error answers with a status and a JSON body:

```json
{"error": "limit must be between 1 and 500", "code": "invalid"}
```

`error` is a sentence in plain words, safe to show to a person; it may change between versions. `code` is stable: branch on it. Codes are only ever added.

| Code | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | The body could not be read as JSON (most routes answer `invalid` instead, with the parser's message) |
| `invalid` | 400 | A parameter or field is wrong; `error` says which and why |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | No key, or one that is unknown, expired or turned off, or whose maker is disabled |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | Wrong username or password (signing in, not in v1) |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The key's access, or its maker's roles, do not allow this on something it can see |
| `api_key_scope` | 403 | The route is outside the key's areas |
| `cross_site` | 403 | A browser request without the CSRF header (sessions only) |
| `not_found` | 404 | It does not exist, or is outside the key's reach |
| `conflict` | 409 | The current state does not allow it, like a silence already over; `error` says why |
| `idempotency_in_progress` | 409 | The first request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running |
| `gone` | 410 | A one-time link that was used or expired (not in v1) |
| `idempotency_key_reused` | 422 | This `Idempotency-Key` was used for another request |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Over the key's rate limit |
| `internal` | 500 | Something failed on the central server; the details are in its log |
| `metrics_unavailable` | 502 | The metrics database is unreachable, failing or not configured |
| `logs_unavailable` | 502 | The logs database is unreachable, failing or not configured |
| `metrics_timeout` | 504 | The metrics database did not answer in time |
| `logs_timeout` | 504 | The logs database did not answer in time |

## Idempotency keys

A `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` made with a key may carry `Idempotency-Key`: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The first request with a value runs and its answer is kept for 24 hours. The same request again (same method, path, query and body) gets that answer back with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of running a second time. A script that lost its connection can then retry without opening two silences or queuing two updates.

- The same value with another request answers 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.
- While the first request is still running, a retry answers 409 `idempotency_in_progress`; try again a moment later.
- Answers of 500 and above are not kept, so a retry runs again. Answers over 1 MiB are not kept either.
- Answers that hand out a secret once (tokens, install keys, signing secrets) are not stored: a replay says it was done, without the secret.
- Values belong to a key: two keys never see each other's answers.

Without the header, writes behave as usual. Most are safe to repeat anyway, like acknowledging an incident or setting a value; the operations that are not say so.

## Rate limits

Each key may make 600 requests a minute, counted in fixed one-minute windows on each central server. Every answer to a key carries:

- `RateLimit-Limit`: requests allowed in a window, 600.
- `RateLimit-Remaining`: requests left in the current window.
- `RateLimit-Reset`: seconds until the window ends.

Over the limit, requests answer 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, in seconds. Requests made in a browser session are not limited.

post.description:
For servers without Internet access: imports a release from its files,
sent as `multipart/form-data` up to 2 GiB in all. The signature of
`SHA256SUMS` is checked against the release keys built into the server
and every file against its checksum, as `agent-release import` does on
the command line. The release is then served to install commands and
agent and relay updates. Audited as `agent_release.import`.

Global administrators only: the release cache serves every customer.
Through an API key: access "Administer", reach everything, the
"updates" area. One import at a time. `Idempotency-Key` is ignored on
this route: importing the same release again replaces it with the same
files.

parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of running twice.

post.summary: Import a release from a URL
post.description:
Like the upload, but the server downloads the release's files from the
directory `url`, over http or https: the signature protects the files,
not the transport. Files the directory does not have (404) are skipped;
the required ones are then reported missing. The download stops after
60 seconds without data, or beyond 2 GiB. Audited as
`agent_release.import`, with only the URL's host.

Global administrators only. Through an API key: access "Administer",
reach everything, the "updates" area. One import at a time; repeating
imports the same release again.

get.summary: Read the progress of automatic updates
get.description:
The settings as they apply, the central server's version (agents and
relays never move past it), and for agents and for relays: the newest
stable release held, the `target` they move to, its rollout, totals,
each site's phase and totals, the last 10 rollouts with their
`outcome`, and `versions`: how many agents or relays run each version,
newest first, which `GET /api/v1/auto-update/{kind}/versions/peers`
lists. Relays are updated before the agents behind them.

MonitorFlow sends each server or relay that needs it a signed
`self_update` command, with no person's approval: one per site first
(`canary`), then a quarter of the site at a time (`rolling`). A site
whose first update failed is `blocked` for that version. Each server is
tried once per version. Only the agent or relay restarts, never the
host, and its watchdog rolls back a version that does not connect.

Needs a global administrator role and the key area "updates".

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off, or whose maker is disabled: `unauthenticated`

403.description: `forbidden`: not a global administrator. `api_key_scope`: the key lacks the area

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`; `Retry-After` says in how many seconds to try again

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the key's window ends.

post.description:
A rollout halts everywhere once `failure_threshold` of its updates
failed. Resuming it, once the cause is fixed, counts failures again
from now, and each blocked site gets a new first server among those
not tried yet; `self_update` commands are sent again at the next pass
(every 5 minutes by default), unless automatic updates are paused.

Needs a global administrator role and the key area "updates". Audited
as `auto_update.resume`. Resuming again is 409.

totals of `GET /api/v1/auto-update`, classified the same way, so `total` equals

get.description:
How available the business services, servers, devices and checks the key reads were over a period, from one hour to 13 months: this month so far when `from` and `to` are absent.

**What counts as down**: any time a critical incident was open: a check failing at its critical threshold, a server offline, or a server unreachable because what it is reached through was down (an offline relay). Warnings never count. **Planned maintenance**, time under a silence or a maintenance window, is given apart (`maintenance_seconds`) and left out of `counted_seconds`; a silence counts from when it started or was made, whichever is later. `availability` is the share of `counted_seconds` that was up, in percent, or `null` when nothing was counted. An outage is one unbroken stretch of down time, with its causes.

Services give their SLA `target`, whether it was `met`, and `budget_seconds`: the down time the target allowed minus the down time there was, negative once exceeded. `checks` lists only checks that had outages. Computed from the incident history on each request, so a past period gives the same numbers later, unless something was removed since.

**Who**: any role. With `customer_id`, only that customer's sites the key reads; business services only of customers the key is granted as a whole. **Area**: `alerts`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start of the period, RFC 3339; the start of this month (UTC) when
absent.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
End of the period, excluded; now when absent. A period still going
on counts until now.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Only this customer's sites and services.

Asks the updater for a backup of the database and the server's data
directory. Answers at once; the backup shows as `last` in
`GET /api/v1/backups` once the updater takes it, and the oldest file
beyond 7 is removed when it ends. Audited as `server.backup`.

Errors: 409 `conflict` when the deployment has no updater, the updater
is not running, or a backup is already running or asked for. A second
request while one runs is refused, so a retry never takes two.

get.description:
The file itself, `application/gzip`, served as an attachment with
`Cache-Control: no-store`; `Range` requests are honoured. It is a tar
archive of `manifest.json` (format, time, server version, latest
migration), `database.dump` (`pg_dump` custom format of the whole
database: every customer's servers, sites, incidents, commands, users
with their password hashes, API key hashes and the audit log) and
`serverdata/`, the server's data directory: the certificate
authority's private key, the key that signs commands to agents, the
key that opens the stored SMTP passwords, webhook secrets and AI key,
and the mirror signing key. Whoever holds the file can read all of
that and act as the central server towards every agent and relay;
keep it as you would those keys.

Only a global administrator, or a key with access "Administer", reach
"Everything" and the "administration" area, may download one. Each
download is audited as `server.backup.download` with the file name.

Errors: 404 `not_found` for a name the updater did not write or a file
already rotated away; 409 `conflict` when the backups volume is not
mounted in the server or only root can read it on the host.

post.description:
Makes a `draft` campaign: nothing is sent to any server until it is
started. Its servers are frozen now: those of `server_ids` and the
unrevoked servers of `site_id`, all of the customer, sorted by host
name. A server added to the site later is not added to the campaign.
They are split into batches by `waves`, in order: explicit server
lists first, then `{"size": n}` and `{"percent": p}` (of all servers,
rounded up) take the next servers by host name; the servers left form
one last batch. Without `waves`, one batch.

Once started, each server gets one signed command, sent when its agent
is connected and has no other command in flight:

- a package update (`apply_updates` with `packages`, `security_only`
  and `allow_reboot`; empty `packages` upgrades everything). A server
  whose agent does not accept package updates is left out of its
  batch. Where it can, MonitorFlow takes a local snapshot of the server
  first (`snapshot_command_id`). With `sources`, the server's package
  sources are first pointed at the pinned mirror snapshots and put back
  after the update (`sources_command_id`, `restore_command_id`); the
  central server needs mirrors and `mirror_public_url` for that;
- or, with `agent_version`, an agent update (`self_update`) to that
  version, which takes no package options.

These commands come from an administrator, so they are not classified
by the risk rules and need no approval.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.create`. Not safe to repeat: send
`Idempotency-Key` to retry.

new one is first only trusted: servers and relays learn to trust it
over their next connections, then it issues once all have moved, then the old one is retired
and its key destroyed, each step taken by the server by itself. In an
emergency the new one issues at once and the old one stops being
trusted 24 hours later: servers and relays that have not connected by
then must be installed again. An emergency request during a planned
change switches it at once. Audited as `ca.rotation.start`; agents and
relays receive the new trust over their next connections, no command
is sent.

Errors: 409 `conflict` when a change is already under way, when more
than one central server instance is running, or when this server has
no certificate authority.

get.description:
What is behind what, among the servers, devices and relays the key reads. A dependency says that a child (a server, a device, or one of its checks) is behind a parent (a server, a device, a relay, or one check such as an uplink ping). While a parent is down, what is behind it opens no incident of its own and notifies nobody: it is unreachable, and the parent's incident speaks for it. Children are judged again 2 minutes after the parent's incident resolves.

A parent is down while its offline incident is open (a server's agent, a relay), while a ping check of it has a critical incident open (a server or device), or, for a check, while that check has a critical incident open.

This lists the dependencies people set; the automatic ones (a server behind its relay, a check behind the relay that runs it) are in `GET /api/v1/servers/{id}/dependencies`.

**Who**: any role. **Area**: `alerts`.

**Filter**: `server_id` for those whose child or parent is that server or device or one of its checks, `relay_id` for those behind that relay. Unknown parameters are 400.

Add more checks with `POST /api/v1/servers/{id}/sensor_configs` and a `probe`.

With `snmp` credentials and a `template` (ADR-0149), it also gets the SNMP checks and thresholds of that kind of device, run from the same probe; `POST /api/v1/devices/detect` suggests the template. The credentials are stored sealed and never returned.

With `vmware` credentials (ADR-0156), a vCenter or ESXi host also gets its `vmware` check every 5 minutes from the same probe, and its alerts; test the connection and confirm its certificate first with `POST /api/v1/devices/vmware/test`.

post.summary: Add a custom SNMP check to a device
post.description:
Watches any objects of the device: 1 to 10 channels, each a numeric OID with its name, optional `key` (the metric suffix, from the name), `type` (`gauge` as read, `counter` for a rate per second from the second reading, or `text`), `unit`, `multiply` or `divide` (tenths of a degree: `divide` 10), `lookup` (`builtin:<name>` or a lookup of the customer, from `GET /api/v1/snmp-lookups`), and for a text `match` (`contains`, `not_contains`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `matches` with a regular expression, `not_matches`), `expect` and `severity` (`warning` or `critical`, the default). With `table` (a table or its entry) and `name_column`, each `oid` is a column, and every row of the table is an instance named by that column; new rows appear by themselves. A channel's `limits` become the device's threshold on its metric; a channel with a lookup or an expected text also gets a rule on its `_state` series, warning at 1 and critical at 2. The check runs from `probe` (the site's relay by default, else the central server) with the device's SNMP credentials, every `interval_ms` (a minute by default). Thresholds, richer rules, silences, dependencies and reports apply to these series like any other.

**Who**: operator or above on the device's site. **Area**: `servers`. Audited as `snmp_check.create`. **Not safe to repeat**: send `Idempotency-Key` to retry.

get.description:
The maintenance windows of the sites the key reads, the next to come first, in full. A maintenance window is a silence that comes back on its own every day, week or month, at local times in a time zone, for a site, chosen servers of it, or chosen checks of those: notifications are held while one runs, exactly as a silence holds them, and what is still open at its end is sent then. It needs no renewing.

Each window lists its next three windows (`next`, the running one first) and, while one runs, when it ends (`active_until`). While one runs, its servers' `silence` says `window: true`, and its incidents `in_maintenance: true`.

**Who**: any role. **Area**: `alerts`.

**Filter**: at most one of `site_id` and `server_id`, for the windows of the site, or those covering the server (its whole site's, and those naming it). Unknown parameters are 400.

post.description:
A silence that comes back on its own:

- `daily`: every `every` days from `starts_on`;
- `weekly`: on `weekdays`, every `every` weeks from the week of `starts_on`;
- `monthly`: on `month_day` (a month without that day has no window), or on the one weekday of `weekdays` in week `month_week` of the month (5 is the last: "the last Friday"), in `months` (every month when absent).

Each window starts at `start_time`, local to `time_zone`, and lasts `duration_minutes` (at most 7 days). Daylight saving is followed: a start that happens twice when clocks go back is the first, one skipped when they go forward is read with the offset before the change, and the end is the local start plus the duration, so "22:00 for 8 hours" ends at 06:00 local time on the nights clocks change.

Without `server_ids`, it covers the whole site, servers added later included. With `checks`, only the incidents those checks write: the server going offline and its other checks still notify.

**Who**: operator or above on the site. **Area**: `alerts`. Audited as `maintenance_window.create`. **Not safe to repeat**: each request makes a window; send `Idempotency-Key` to retry.

Adds an administrator rule to the classifier of a customer, or of one
of its sites. It applies to the next command the AI proposes on the
servers it covers; nothing is sent to agents. A command already waiting
for approval keeps its tier, but is classified again when approved.

- `allow`: a command no built-in rule knows, matching `pattern` as a
  whole, gets `tier`, `read_only` (runs without approval) or
  `low_impact` (needs approval unless the site's policy lets it run).
  An allow rule never applies to a command a built-in rule decides,
  and its program may not be one the built-in rules reserve (`sudo`,
  shells and interpreters, package managers, `systemctl`, `rm`,
  `kill`, `reboot` and the like): that is 400.
- `deny`: a command containing a match anywhere, after `;`, `&&`, `|`
  too, is `forbidden`, whatever the other rules say. Deny wins over
  every allow rule.
- `cache_dir`: `find <pattern> -mindepth 1 -delete` becomes a
  low-impact command for that directory.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "remediation". Audited as `remediation_rule.create`. Not safe to
repeat with a different body; the same rule twice is 409.

put.description:
Replaces every field of a site's or a server's row; fields left out take their defaults. The row stays on its site or server. Safe to repeat.

**Who**: operator or above ("Read and change") on the row's site. **Area**: `alerts`.

Rows are checked as the agent checks them: `kind` must be a sensor it knows, `params` only the settings of that kind, with valid values, and `interval_ms` 10 s to 24 h. A `plugin` row names a check plugin turned on for the site in `params.plugin`. The answer to a bad row is 400 `invalid`, saying what is wrong. A second row with the same `name` and `instance` for the same site or server is 409.

A server's own row may name a `probe` (ADR-0148): `central` for the central server, or the ID of a relay of the server's site, which then runs it instead of the agent. Probes run `ping`, `port` (TCP or UDP) and `http` checks; a device's rows always have one, and default to the relay of its site, else the central server. A probe check of a server with an agent names its `host`; a device's checks default to its address. A website check names its `url` and takes no address. Its `instance` defaults to the probe's key (`central` or the relay's name), so two probes watching one address keep apart. `ping` and UDP never run on an agent.

A website check is kind `http` (ADR-0150): `params.url` and optional `method`, `status`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `follow_redirects`, `headers`, `username`, `password` and `ip`. `password` is sent only over `https://`, kept sealed and never returned: rows say `secret_set` instead; an update without it keeps the stored one, and `""` removes it. Its last runs are read with `GET /api/v1/servers/{id}/website-checks`.

A custom SNMP check of a device is kind `snmp_custom` (ADR-0157), run by a probe with the device's credentials: up to 10 channels, `oidN` (a numeric OID) with optional `nameN`, `keyN` (the metric suffix, from the name), `typeN` (`gauge`, `counter` for a rate per second, or `text`), `unitN`, `multiplyN`, `divideN`, `lookupN` (`builtin:<name>` or the ID of a lookup of the customer) and, for a text, `matchN` (`contains`, `not_contains`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `matches`, `not_matches`), `expectN` and `severityN` (`warning` or `critical`); or a `table` OID with a `name_column`, each `oidN` then a column of it. Credentials and `lookupN_map` are refused: they are added when the check is sent to its probe. `/api/v1/devices/{id}/snmp-checks` reads and writes the same rows with their thresholds.

Audited as `sensor_config.create`, `sensor_config.update` or `sensor_config.delete`, with the names of the parameters but never their values. Connected agents get the change within seconds.

post.summary: Add a sensor row to a server
post.description:
Adds a sensor to one server, or replaces for it the sensor of the same name and instance that its site or the built-in checks give; with `enabled: false`, removes that sensor from it.

**Who**: operator or above ("Read and change") on the server's site. **Area**: `alerts`.

Rows are checked as the agent checks them: `kind` must be a sensor it knows, `params` only the settings of that kind, with valid values, and `interval_ms` 10 s to 24 h. A `plugin` row names a check plugin turned on for the site in `params.plugin`. The answer to a bad row is 400 `invalid`, saying what is wrong. A second row with the same `name` and `instance` for the same site or server is 409.

A server's own row may name a `probe` (ADR-0148): `central` for the central server, or the ID of a relay of the server's site, which then runs it instead of the agent. Probes run `ping`, `port` (TCP or UDP) and `http` checks; a device's rows always have one, and default to the relay of its site, else the central server. A probe check of a server with an agent names its `host`; a device's checks default to its address. A website check names its `url` and takes no address. Its `instance` defaults to the probe's key (`central` or the relay's name), so two probes watching one address keep apart. `ping` and UDP never run on an agent.

A website check is kind `http` (ADR-0150): `params.url` and optional `method`, `status`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `follow_redirects`, `headers`, `username`, `password` and `ip`. `password` is sent only over `https://`, kept sealed and never returned: rows say `secret_set` instead; an update without it keeps the stored one, and `""` removes it. Its last runs are read with `GET /api/v1/servers/{id}/website-checks`.

A custom SNMP check of a device is kind `snmp_custom` (ADR-0157), run by a probe with the device's credentials: up to 10 channels, `oidN` (a numeric OID) with optional `nameN`, `keyN` (the metric suffix, from the name), `typeN` (`gauge`, `counter` for a rate per second, or `text`), `unitN`, `multiplyN`, `divideN`, `lookupN` (`builtin:<name>` or the ID of a lookup of the customer) and, for a text, `matchN` (`contains`, `not_contains`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `matches`, `not_matches`), `expectN` and `severityN` (`warning` or `critical`); or a `table` OID with a `name_column`, each `oidN` then a column of it. Credentials and `lookupN_map` are refused: they are added when the check is sent to its probe. `/api/v1/devices/{id}/snmp-checks` reads and writes the same rows with their thresholds.

Audited as `sensor_config.create`, `sensor_config.update` or `sensor_config.delete`, with the names of the parameters but never their values. Connected agents get the change within seconds.

post.summary: Add a threshold row to a server
post.description:
Sets a threshold for one server, replacing for it the one of the same metric and instance that its site or the built-in thresholds give; with `enabled: false`, turns that threshold off for it.

**Who**: operator or above ("Read and change") on the server's site. **Area**: `alerts`.

`metric` is `monitorflow_` followed by a sensor's metric name. An enabled row needs `warning` or `critical`, and `critical` must be on the alarm side of `warning` (above it for `>` and `>=`, below it for `<` and `<=`); `duration_s` is 0 to 86400 and `hysteresis` 0 or more. A bad row is 400 `invalid`, saying what is wrong; a second row with the same `metric`, `instance` and `kind` for the same site or server is 409.

`kind` says what is judged (ADR-0153), with only the fields it uses: `value` (the default) the sample; `window` a `function` (`avg`, `min`, `max`, `change`, `rate` per second) over `window_s` (60 to 86400); `compare` the average over `window_s` (300 to 86400) against `offset_s` earlier (86400 or 604800), as a `ratio` or a `difference`; `forecast` the seconds left until the value reaches `target` on the side `comparison` names, learned over `window_s` (3600 to 604800), with `warning` and `critical` in seconds left (critical the shorter); `nodata` the seconds since the last sample arrived, with `warning` and `critical` in seconds (60 to 604800), no `duration_s` and no `comparison` but `>`. Up to two `conditions` joined with "and" read other metrics of the same server (not for `nodata`). Use `POST .../thresholds/preview` to see what a rule would have done.

Audited as `threshold.create`, `threshold.update` or `threshold.delete`. MonitorFlow applies the change within seconds; an open incident's `threshold` still shows the values it opened with.

post.summary: Add a sensor row to a site
post.description:
Adds a sensor to every server of the site, or replaces the built-in sensor of the same name and instance; with `enabled: false`, removes it. A server's own row still wins over the site's.

**Who**: operator or above ("Read and change") on the site. **Area**: `alerts`.

Rows are checked as the agent checks them: `kind` must be a sensor it knows, `params` only the settings of that kind, with valid values, and `interval_ms` 10 s to 24 h. A `plugin` row names a check plugin turned on for the site in `params.plugin`. The answer to a bad row is 400 `invalid`, saying what is wrong. A second row with the same `name` and `instance` for the same site or server is 409.

A server's own row may name a `probe` (ADR-0148): `central` for the central server, or the ID of a relay of the server's site, which then runs it instead of the agent. Probes run `ping`, `port` (TCP or UDP) and `http` checks; a device's rows always have one, and default to the relay of its site, else the central server. A probe check of a server with an agent names its `host`; a device's checks default to its address. A website check names its `url` and takes no address. Its `instance` defaults to the probe's key (`central` or the relay's name), so two probes watching one address keep apart. `ping` and UDP never run on an agent.

A website check is kind `http` (ADR-0150): `params.url` and optional `method`, `status`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `follow_redirects`, `headers`, `username`, `password` and `ip`. `password` is sent only over `https://`, kept sealed and never returned: rows say `secret_set` instead; an update without it keeps the stored one, and `""` removes it. Its last runs are read with `GET /api/v1/servers/{id}/website-checks`.

A custom SNMP check of a device is kind `snmp_custom` (ADR-0157), run by a probe with the device's credentials: up to 10 channels, `oidN` (a numeric OID) with optional `nameN`, `keyN` (the metric suffix, from the name), `typeN` (`gauge`, `counter` for a rate per second, or `text`), `unitN`, `multiplyN`, `divideN`, `lookupN` (`builtin:<name>` or the ID of a lookup of the customer) and, for a text, `matchN` (`contains`, `not_contains`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `matches`, `not_matches`), `expectN` and `severityN` (`warning` or `critical`); or a `table` OID with a `name_column`, each `oidN` then a column of it. Credentials and `lookupN_map` are refused: they are added when the check is sent to its probe. `/api/v1/devices/{id}/snmp-checks` reads and writes the same rows with their thresholds.

post.description:
Makes a single-use token that enrolls one server (`agent`) or relay
(`relay`) under the ID `peer_id` on the site `site_id`. The answer is
the only time the secret `token` is shown: MonitorFlow stores its hash,
no route returns it again, and a token that is lost is revoked and made
again. It comes with what the install commands need: the addresses to
enroll at and connect to, and where installers download the agent from.

For a relay, `server_names` are the names and addresses its agents reach
it at; they go on its certificate. A relay token without them leaves
the relay waiting for an administrator to confirm its names (`POST
/api/v1/relays/{id}/names`).

cannot read is 404. Audited as `enrollment_token.create`, without the
secret.

`Idempotency-Key`, a repeat does not make a second one but answers 409
`conflict` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, saying the secret is shown
only once: the first answer is not stored.

`check`: an incident of a check; `offline`: the server stopped
reporting; `unreachable`: what it is reached through was down
(`via`); `member`: a member of a business service was down.

via.description: What it depends on, for `unreachable`: a relay's name.

device.description: A device, watched from a probe, rather than a server with an agent.

checks.description: Only these checks of them; empty for all of them.

servers.description: What it covered: servers and devices of the report, by name.

window.description: An occurrence of a maintenance window.

AvailabilityMember.description: A member of a business service, by name.

AvailabilityNumbers.description: The numbers of one thing over the period.

availability.description:
Percentage of the counted time that was up, 0 to 100; `null` when
nothing was counted (all of it planned maintenance).

counted_seconds.description: The period without planned maintenance, seconds.

maintenance_seconds.description: Planned maintenance, left out of the count, seconds.

causes.description: What was down, the earliest first.

ongoing.description: Whether it was still going on when the report was made.

checks.description: Only checks that had outages; the others were up all along.

customer_id.description: The customer it is for; `null` for everything the reader sees.

budget_seconds.description:
The down time the target allowed, minus the down time there was,
seconds; negative when it was exceeded.

met.description:
Whether the target was met; `null` without a target or when
nothing was counted.

target.description: The SLA target, a percentage; `null` without one.

AvailabilitySummary.description: The overall line of a report.

maintenance_seconds.description: Planned maintenance of the period, its own time once.

outages.description: Outages of servers and devices, and their down time in all.

AvailableRelease.description:
A release newer than the running server, as `GET /api/server-update`
shows it.

first_seen_at.description: When a check first saw it.

BackupArchive.description: A backup file: a gzip-compressed tar archive.

name.description: `monitorflow-backup-<UTC time>-<kind>.tar.gz`, the name to download.

BackupKind.description: Why a backup was taken; part of its file name.

error.description: Why it failed, in plain words; `null` unless `failed`.

id.description: The request's ID for one asked for, else the updater's own.

warning.description: What a backup that succeeded left out or noticed.

id.description: The request's ID: the `last.id` of the backup once the updater takes it.

Backups.description:
The backups part of `status.json`. Missing in the status of an updater
older than backups.

oneOf.description: The last backup, running or finished, of any kind.

last_success_at.description: When the last one that succeeded finished.

next_at.description: When the next automatic one is due.

downloads.description: The backups volume is mounted: files can be downloaded.

enabled.description: The server shares a volume with the updater, which takes backups.

host_dir.description:
Backups are mounted but only root can read them: they are in a
host directory, `BACKUP_DIR`, and are copied from there.

requested.description: "Back up now" waits for the updater to take it.

updater_alive.description: The updater reported within the last two minutes.

can_change.description: Whether this user may change or remove it.

oneOf.description: The check; `null` for the whole server or device.

BusinessServiceMemberRequest.description: A member in a request: a whole server or device, or one check of it.

oneOf.description: Only this check of it; absent or `null` for the whole server.

BusinessServiceRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/business-services` and `PUT
/api/business-services/{id}`; a change replaces every field.

at_least.description: For `at_least`: 1 to the number of members.

customer_id.description: The customer it belongs to; may be left out when there is only one.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters, unique per customer, like `Email`.

rule.description:
`all` (the default): down while any member is down; `at_least`: down
while fewer than `at_least` members are up.

target.description:
The SLA target, a percentage from 50 to 100 with up to three
decimals, like 99.9; absent or `null` for none.

CaPeer.description: Where an enrolled peer stands, from its newest certificate.

cut_off.description:
Its certificate comes from a CA the server no longer trusts: it
missed an emergency change and must be installed again.

moved.description: Its certificate comes from the CA that issues now.

name.description: The host name of a server, the name of a relay.

not_after.description: When its certificate expires: it stops counting then.

too_old.description: Its version takes no CA bundle: it must update first.

trusts_all.description: It trusts every CA the server trusts.

CaRotation.description: A change of certificate authority under way.

distrust_at.description: Emergency: when the old CA stops being trusted.

done.description: Those done with the current step.

emergency.description:
Started after a suspected compromise: the old CA is distrusted 24
hours after the switch.

other_fingerprint.description: The new CA while introduced, the old one once switched.

stage.description:
`introduced`: servers and relays learn to trust the new CA, the old
one still issues. `switched`: the new one issues, the old one is
still trusted until it is retired.

total.description: Servers and relays with a valid certificate.

waiting.description: Those not done, by name, up to 50, last seen first.

emergency.description:
`true` after a suspected compromise of the CA's key: the new CA
issues at once and the old one is distrusted 24 hours later.
Default `false`: a planned change, one step at a time.

CaStage.description: The step a change of certificate authority is at.

CaView.description: The certificate authority that issues now, and any change under way.

auto_change_at.description: When a planned change starts by itself if nobody starts one.

cut_off.description:
Servers and relays whose certificate comes from a CA no longer
trusted: they missed an emergency change and must be installed
again. Up to 50.

expires_soon.description: Less than a year left: time to change it.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the CA certificate, lower-case hex.

restored_retired_at.description: Set when a restore brought back a CA this server had retired.

oneOf.description: The change under way; `null` when none is.

agent_version.description: Set for an agent update campaign (ADR-0053).

command_ttl_s.description: Seconds a command may wait for its agent.

created_by.description: The user who made it; `null` once that user is deleted.

current_wave.description:
Index of the batch in progress, from 0; `null` before the first is
queued.

error.description: Why it stopped or failed; `null` otherwise.

site_id.description: The site named at creation; `null` when only `server_ids` were.

oneOf.description: The pinned snapshots, if any (ADR-0038).

spec.description: What every package update installs (unused by an agent update).

CampaignDetail.description: `GET /api/campaigns/{id}` and the answer of every write.

CampaignFailureThreshold.description:
A wave fails when more of its servers failed than this. A failed
server is a command `failed`, `expired` or `cancelled`, or a server
skipped with an error. The default, `{"value": 0, "unit": "count"}`,
stops at the first failure.

CampaignFailureUnit.description: How a failure threshold counts: servers, or percent of the batch.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

CampaignPinnedMirror.description: A mirror and the published snapshot a campaign pins it to.

name.description: The mirror's name.

snapshot.description: One of its published snapshots, not `current`.

CampaignProgress.description:
Servers by status; `failed` includes expired commands and skipped
servers, `in_progress` queued, sent and running commands.

CampaignRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/campaigns`. Only `customer_id`, `name` and a target
(`site_id` and/or `server_ids`) are required.

agent_version.description:
Update the agents to this version, like `0.3.1`, instead of
packages (ADR-0053); takes no package options nor `sources`.

allow_reboot.description: Whether the agent may reboot the server when an update needs it.

command_ttl_s.description:
Seconds a command may wait for its agent before it expires, 60 to
604800, default 3600; never past the end of the open window.

include_os.description:
Whether OS updates are included; true by default. Without them,
only servers of a platform a selected manager is for are targets
(ADR-0138).

packages.description:
Packages to upgrade, up to 1000; empty upgrades everything. Names
are letters, digits and `.+_:-` not starting with `-`, or KB
numbers and update IDs for Windows servers.

server_ids.description: These servers of the customer, besides those of `site_id`.

site_id.description: Every unrevoked server of this site of the customer.

oneOf.description: Snapshots to pin every server to during its update (ADR-0038).

third_party.description:
Third-party managers to update after the OS, each once:
`[{"manager": "winget" | "flatpak" | "snap", "packages": [id]}]`,
empty `packages` for every pending app (ADR-0138).

waves.description:
The batches, in order, up to 100; the servers left over make one
last batch. Empty: one batch of every server.

command_id.description:
The update command, see `/commands/{id}`; `null` before it is
queued.

exit_code.description: The update's exit code once it ran, else `null`.

snapshot_command_id.description: The local snapshot taken before the update, if any (ADR-0094).

sources_command_id.description:
With pinned snapshots: the `configure_sources` command before the
update and the command restoring the sources after it.

status.description:
`pending` (no command yet), `skipped` (no command, `error` says
why), or the command's state: `queued`, `sent`, `running`,
`succeeded`, `failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`. A failed restore of
pinned sources makes it `failed`.

CampaignSources.description:
The snapshots every server of a campaign installs from (ADR-0038):
each server uses the mirrors of its OS family.

mirrors.description: One or more mirrors, each once. Windows servers take no sources.

CampaignSourcesMode.description: How pinned sources treat a host's other sources (ADR-0032).

CampaignState.description: Where a campaign is. `stopped`, `completed` and `failed` are final.

CampaignUpdateSpec.description: The `ApplyUpdates` of every command of a campaign.

allow_reboot.description: Whether the agent may reboot the server when an update needs it.

include_os.description:
Whether the OS's own updates are included; true by default
(ADR-0138).

packages.description: OS packages to upgrade; empty upgrades everything.

security_only.description:
Only security updates of the OS. Third-party managers have no
security classification: they are included whole or not at all.

third_party.description: Third-party managers to update, after the OS (ADR-0138).

oneOf.description: These servers of the campaign, `{"servers": [...]}`.
The next `n` servers by host name, `{"size": n}`.

size.description: The next `n` servers by host name, `{"size": n}`.

oneOf.description:
The next servers, `p` percent of all of them rounded up (1 to 100),
`{"percent": p}`.

percent.description:
The next servers, `p` percent of all of them rounded up (1 to 100),
`{"percent": p}`.

CampaignWaveSpec.description:
One wave as requested: explicit servers, a number of servers, or a
percentage of all targets (rounded up), taken in target order from
those no explicit wave names.

oneOf.description:
Every week on `weekdays` (ISO: 1 is Monday, 7 Sunday), from `start`
to `end` local time in `timezone` (IANA name). An `end` before
`start` closes the next day.

end.description: `HH:MM`, local time; `00:00` and `24:00` are the end of the day.

oneOf.description: Once, from `starts_at` to `ends_at`.

CampaignWindow.description:
When a campaign may queue commands. With no window, at any time; with
several, whenever one is open. At most 32.

added.description: Every mirror of the distribution exists.

index_bytes.description: What on demand needs at least: the indexes, in bytes.

name.description: Its name on screen, such as `Debian 12`.

on_demand_problem.description:
Why it cannot be added on demand now: too little free space even
for its indexes.

on_demand_size_bytes.description:
About what they take on demand (ADR-0142): indexes and the packages
a fleet typically installs, in bytes.

problem.description: Why it cannot be added in full mode now: too little free space.

size_bytes.description: About what its mirrors take on disk in full mode, in bytes.

CentralRelease.description:
The newest cached release as `central` install commands pin it
(ADR-0054): its version and the SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS`, of the
installer and of the MSI, as hex. A file is only named when the cache
holds it.

installer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of `install.sh`; `null` when the cache lacks it.

msi_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the Windows MSI; `null` when the cache lacks it.

path.description:
URL path of its files behind the web interface, without a
trailing slash: `/agent/<version>`.

Certificate.description: The certificate of a website check's last https connection.

ok.description: Trusted, valid now and for the name.

label.description:
The server, and the instance when there are several, or how the
servers combine.

points.description:
`[unix seconds, value]` every `step`; the value is `null` where
nothing was reported.

server_id.description: The server of a line per server; absent when combined.

CheckInterval.description: Body of the request and of the answer.

interval_ms.description:
Milliseconds, 10000 (10 s) to 86400000 (24 h); `null` or absent:
the built-in interval, every minute.

dismissed_by.description: Who dismissed it and when; null while it stands.

reported_at.description:
When the agent last reported what runs; null before its first
report, or for an agent that does not report (Windows, older).

channel.description:
The channel checked: `tested` while a license key is valid,
`regular` otherwise (ADR-0147).

error.description: Why there is no `latest`.

oneOf.description: `null` when the release could not be fetched or verified.

reachable.description: Whether the source answered; `false` on an offline server.

source.description: Base URL releases are fetched from.

CheckUsage.description: One check and how many servers run it.

kind.description: The kind of check, like `port`, `systemd` or `plugin`.

name.description: The sensor name, like `port_443` or `service_nginx`.

plugin.description: For kind `plugin`, the plugin it runs.

servers.description: Servers that run it, not removed ones.

reason.description: One sentence for the approval queue and the audit log.

rule.description:
The rule that decided: `{"source": "builtin", "id": "readonly.df"}`
or `{"source": "configured", "id": "<rule UUID>"}`.

oneOf.description: A built-in rule, by its stable ID such as `readonly.df`.
A row of `remediation_rules`.

command.description:
The command line, as the AI would propose it. Neither stored nor
logged.

shell.description:
`posix` (the default) for Linux servers, `powershell` for Windows
ones (ADR-0084).

site_id.description:
The site whose rules apply as well; `null` or absent for the
customer-wide rules only.

stderr.description: The last 64 KiB of its errors; `null` until the agent sends them.

stdout.description: The last 64 KiB of its output; `null` until the agent sends it.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

allow_reboot.description: `apply_updates`: reboot when an update needs it.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

include_os.description:
`apply_updates`: include the OS's own updates; true by default
(ADR-0138).

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

third_party.description:
`apply_updates`: third-party managers to update after the OS, each
once (ADR-0138). Needs an agent that reports third-party apps.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

campaign_id.description: The update campaign it belongs to, if any.

error.description: Why it failed or expired, in plain words; `null` otherwise.

exit_code.description: The process's exit code; `null` until it ends, or when it never ran.

expires_at.description: The agent does not start it after this; it is then `expired`.

kind.description:
`apply_updates`, `self_update`, `configure_sources`,
`revert_sources`, `shell` (AI remediation), `ai_commands`, or
`take_snapshot` and `delete_snapshot` (local snapshots before AI
changes).

parameters.description:
What it asks, as JSON, by kind: `{"packages", "security_only",
"allow_reboot", "include_os", "third_party"}` for `apply_updates`, `{"version", "base_urls",
"allow_downgrade", "health_timeout_seconds"}` for `self_update`,
`{"mirror_base_url", "family", "mode", "repositories",
"key_fingerprints"}` for `configure_sources`, `{}` for
`revert_sources`, `{"command", "timeout_seconds"}` for `shell`,
`{"on"}` for `ai_commands`; `null` for a kind this version does not
know.

requested_by.description:
The user who queued it, a key's maker included; `null` for
MonitorFlow itself (AI remediation, campaigns, automatic updates).

mirrors.description: 1 to 32 mirrors of the server's package family.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the command waits for the server, 60 to 604800; 3600 by
default.

address.description:
The address in `upstream_url` and `enroll_url`, which the tokens
page lets administrators change.

install.description: The install sources and the default one (ADR-0054).

token.description:
The secret: `mfe1.`, 43 characters of base64url, `.`, and the
pinned SHA-256 of the certificate authority in 43 more. Shown in
this answer only; MonitorFlow keeps only its hash.

CreatedEnrollmentToken.description:
Body of `POST /api/tokens`: the stored token, its secret string and the
peer configuration it needs. Shown once; nothing returns it again. No
`Debug`, so the secret cannot end up in a log line.

install.description: The install sources and the default one.

token.description:
The secret, in the same `mfe1.…` form as an enrollment token. Shown
in this answer only; MonitorFlow keeps only its hash.

CreatedInstallKey.description:
Body of `POST /api/install-keys`: the stored key, its secret string,
named `token` as installers take it, and what the commands need. Shown
once; no `Debug`, so the secret cannot end up in a log line.

name.description: Unique.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

in_maintenance.description:
Whether a maintenance window covers it now: "In maintenance until
04:00".

silenced_until.description:
When the last silence covering it ends, if one does now (ADR-0079,
ADR-0151).

at.description: When figures and top lists were read.

now.description:
The server's clock when it answered, so a screen with a wrong
clock still shows the right time (ADR-0099).

start.description: The charts' range and step, unix seconds.

panels.description: At most 24, checked as when saving.

within.description:
The dashboard's sharing: a site's or customer's dashboard shows
only its servers.

DashboardRange.description: Time ranges, as on the sensor pages (ADR-0020).

name.description: 1 to 80 characters.

revision.description: The revision the edit started from; `PUT` only.

oneOf.description: Only me: its owner.

name.description: The site's or customer's name; absent for `personal`.

DashboardSharingView.description: [`Sharing`] with the name of the site or customer, for display.

DashboardSpec.description: The stored content of a dashboard.

panels.description: At most 24, in the order shown.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change and delete it.

can_link.description: Whether the user may make display links for it (ADR-0099).

DashboardWithin.description:
The servers a dashboard can show at most: everything the viewer reads,
or one site or customer of it.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

edited.description: Whether an edited command runs instead of the proposal.

Dependencies.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/{id}/dependencies` and
`GET /api/relays/{id}/dependencies`: what its page shows.

behind.description: Everything behind it, directly or through others.

can_change.description: Whether the caller may add and remove its dependencies.

children.description: What depends directly on it or one of its checks.

parents.description: What it, or one of its checks, depends on, automatic ones included.

suggestions.description: Parents that look obvious and are not set.

oneOf.description: While a parent is down; `null` otherwise.

unreachable_checks.description: Its checks that are unreachable while it is not.

automatic.description: A server behind its relay, or a check behind the relay that runs it.

can_change.description: Whether the caller may remove it.

created_by.description:
Who added it; `null` for an automatic one, an import's without a
person, or once the account is removed.

id.description: `null` for an automatic one, which cannot be removed.

DependencyCheck.description: A check of a server or device, by its name and what it watches.

instance.description: What it watches, `""` (the default) for every instance.

name.description: The check's name, like `ping` or `service_nginx`.

DependencyEnd.description: One end of a dependency, named.

oneOf.description: One of its checks; `null` for all of it.

name.description: Its host name, or the relay's name.

server_id.description: The server or device; `null` for a relay.

DependencyEndRequest.description:
One end of a dependency in a request: a server or device, one of its
checks, or (for a parent only) a relay.

oneOf.description: One check of `server_id` instead of all of it.

children.description: At most 500, all added or none.

DependencySuggestion.description: A parent that looks obvious; never added without being asked.

address.description: An IP address or a DNS name.

probe.description: `central` or a relay of the site; absent: the site's default.

Detected.description: What an address answered over SNMP.

answers.description: Whether it answered at all with these credentials.

error.description: Why not, in words; `null` when it answered.

template.description: The template that fits it; `null` when it did not answer.

address.description: Where its checks reach it: an IP address or a DNS name.

name.description:
What people call it, like `Core switch`: 1 to 128 characters
without control characters. Its ID is made from it.

ping.description:
Whether to add a ping every minute, with the thresholds that come
with it: critical when it gets no answer for 2 minutes, a warning
above 20% packet loss for 5 minutes. `true` by default.

probe.description:
Where its ping runs from: `central`, or the ID of a relay of the
site. Absent: the relay of the site when there is one, else the
central server.

site_id.description: The site it is in; its relays can check it.

oneOf.description:
How to reach it over SNMP (ADR-0149); needed with `template`.
Stored sealed, never returned.

template.description:
The kind of device, whose SNMP checks and thresholds it gets, run
from the same probe as its ping: `switch`, `router`, `firewall`,
`printer`, `ups`, `nas` or `generic`. See
`GET /api/devices/templates`, and `POST /api/devices/detect` for the
one that fits.

oneOf.description:
For a vCenter or a standalone ESXi host (ADR-0156): how its probe
logs in, with a Read-only account. The device then gets its
`vmware` check every 5 minutes from the same probe as its ping,
with the alerts that come with it. Test it first with
`POST /api/devices/vmware/test`. Stored sealed, never returned.

DeviceUpdate.description: Body of `PUT /api/devices/{id}`: what changes, the rest stays.

Disk.description: Space of the file system holding `path`.

free_bytes.description: What an unprivileged process can still use, in bytes.

EffectiveSensor.description: One sensor as the agent receives it.

entry_id.description: The row it comes from; `null` for a built-in default.

params.description: As sent to the agent: every value is a string.

probe.description:
Who runs it (ADR-0148): `null` for the agent, `central` or
`relay`; probe checks come after the agent's.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds; `null`: one that grows with the interval.

applied_at.description: When it acknowledged it; `null` if it never did.

applied_revision.description: Revision the agent last acknowledged, `null` if it never did.

check_interval_ms.description: Interval of the built-in checks, in milliseconds (ADR-0097).

in_sync.description: Whether the agent acknowledged the current revision.

EffectiveThreshold.description: One effective threshold, or a muted one, with the layer it comes from.

enabled.description: `false`: muted by a disabled row, which the engine skips.

hysteresis.description: The recovery margin, in the unit of the limits.

threshold_id.description: The row it comes from; `null` for a built-in default.

recommended.description: Suggestions for the site, which its servers would get.

revision.description: Revision the engine compares to reload the server's thresholds.

thresholds.description: By metric and instance, muted ones included.

EnrollmentToken.description: One token, never with its secret.

created_by.description: `null` for tokens made with the server CLI.

created_by_username.description:
`null` for tokens made with the server CLI, or when that user was
deleted.

peer_id.description: The ID the enrolled server or relay gets.

server_names.description:
Relay tokens: the names its certificate will carry. Empty for
agents.

used_at.description: When a host enrolled with it; `null` while unused.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

peer_id.description:
The ID the server or relay will have: its certificate name, 1 to 64
ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. An ID another server or
relay holds is refused.

server_names.description:
Relays only, at most 16: the DNS names and IP addresses its agents
connect to, which its certificate will carry. The central server's
own names and names another site's relay holds are refused. Empty
for agents.

site_id.description: The site it joins.

ttl_s.description:
Validity in seconds, 60 to 604800 (7 days); 3600 (one hour) when
absent or `null`.

EnrollmentTokenState.description: `pending` until used or expired; a used token stays `used`.

Error.description: Every error: a sentence to show and a stable code to branch on.

code.description: Stable; codes are only ever added.

error.description: Plain words, safe to show; may change between versions.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

id.description: Increasing in the order events happened.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

value.description: The metric's value then; `null` when the event has none.

FollowUpChoice.description: A schedule or channel a step may name.

customer_id.description:
The customer it is for, set only for a whole customer; `null`
for a site or everything.

name.description: Its name, or a channel's label.

site_id.description: The site it is for; `null` for a customer or everything.

FollowUpNamed.description: Something a step names, with its name now.

name.description:
Its name now: a schedule's name, a username, or a channel's label;
`null` once removed.

FollowUpPolicy.description: A follow-up as the screen shows it.

customer_id.description:
The customer it covers, or the customer of its site; `null` for
everything.

NetworkScanAdded.description: A device added from a scan.

NetworkScanHost.description: One address that answered, and what the scan proposes for it.

mac.description: Its MAC address, when it is on the probe's own link.

name.description: Its name from reverse DNS.

new.description: Whether it did not answer in the previous finished run.

ping.description: Whether it answered ping, and its round trip.

snmp.description: Whether it answered SNMP, and what it said: shown as text.

NetworkScanProposal.description: What a scan proposes for one address.

action.description:
`agent` (install the agent: SSH or RDP is open), `snmp_device`
(a device with the checks of its template), `device` (a device
with its ping and ports), `monitored` (the site watches it
already) or `dismissed`.

checks.description: What a device added from it is checked with.

oneOf.description: For `monitored`.

name.description:
The name a device added from it gets: the SNMP name, else the
reverse DNS name, else the address.

os.description:
For `agent`: `linux` when SSH is open, `windows` when RDP or WinRM
is.

template.description: For an SNMP device: the template detection suggests.

NetworkScanProposedCheck.description: A check a device added from the proposal gets.

name.description: The check's name: `ping`, `port_443`, `snmp_if`...

every.description:
`hour`, `day` or `week` to scan again on its own; absent or
`null`: only when asked.

name.description: What people call it, like `Office network`.

notify.description:
Whether a run that finds something new or gone sends a
notification to the site's channels. Off by default.

probe.description:
Where it runs from: `central`, or the ID of a relay of the site.
Absent: the relay of the site when there is one, else the central
server.

run.description: Whether to scan now. `true` by default.

site_id.description: The site whose addresses it scans.

oneOf.description:
SNMP credentials to try besides those the site's devices have.
Stored sealed, never returned.

targets.description:
IP addresses, blocks like `192.168.1.0/24` and ranges like
`192.168.1.10-50` or `192.168.1.10-192.168.1.50`: at most 64
entries and 1,024 addresses in all. Never names. Loopback,
multicast, link-local and unspecified addresses are refused;
network and broadcast addresses of IPv4 blocks are left out.

oneOf.description: A run queued or running now, if any.
The latest finished run, whose hosts these are; `null` before one.

addresses.description: Addresses to try, and tried so far.

compared.description:
Whether a finished run came before it, so `new` and `gone` mean
something.

dropped.description:
Answers of the probe that were not believed: an address or port it
was not asked about, a name that does not fit.

error.description:
Why it failed: `interrupted` (the central server instance running
it stopped), `relay_disconnected`, `relay_outdated` (the relay
does not run scans yet: update it), `relay_removed`, or the
probe's own words.

gone.description:
Addresses that answered in the previous finished run and not in
this one.

new.description: Addresses that answered and not in the previous finished run.

ping_error.description:
Why the probe could not ping, when it could not; ports and SNMP
were still tried.

NetworkScanSkipped.description: An address that was not added, and why.

reason.description:
`not_found` (it did not answer in the latest finished run),
`monitored` (the site watches it already), `no_credentials` (the
SNMP credentials that answered are gone; add it by hand).

NetworkScanSnmp.description: A scan's own SNMP credentials, without secrets.

NetworkScanUpdate.description: Body of `PUT /api/network-scans/{id}`: the whole scan but its site.

oneOf.description:
New credentials; absent keeps the stored ones, and a secret left
out keeps the stored one while the version stays.

NotificationChannel.description:
A channel as the web interface shows it. Never its secret: a
webhook shows only its origin, and `has_secret` says whether a
password, signing secret or chat webhook URL is stored.

customer_id.description:
The customer it covers, or the customer of the site it covers;
`null` for everything.

follow_up_only.description:
Hears only follow-up steps that name it, and their resolution
(ADR-0082).

has_secret.description: Whether a password, signing secret or chat webhook URL is stored.

last_error.description: The last delivery's or test's error, `null` once one works.

last_sent_at.description: The last message that went through; `null` before the first.

settings.description:
email: `{"host", "port", "username", "from", "to"}`; webhook:
`{"origin"}`, the URL's scheme, host and port (ADR-0123); chat:
`{"name", "host"}`; plugin: `{"plugin", "name", "values"}`, its
secret settings apart (ADR-0103).

site_id.description: The site it covers; `null` for a whole customer or everything.

NotificationChannelRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/notifications/channels` and of `PUT` on one.

customer_id.description: The customer to cover; with `site_id` also `null`, everything.

follow_up_only.description:
Only follow-up steps that name it, not every event it covers
(ADR-0082).

secret.description:
The SMTP password, webhook signing secret or chat webhook URL, or
a plugin's secret settings as a JSON object of strings; at most
1024 bytes. Write-only: never returned. On `PUT`, absent, `null`
or empty keeps the stored one.

settings.description:
email: `{"host", "port" (587 when absent), "username" (empty
without authentication), "from" (the username when empty), "to"
(1 to 20 addresses)}`; webhook: `{"url"}`, http or https without
a user or password, empty on `PUT` to keep the stored one; chat:
`{"name"}`, at most 80 characters, the URL going in `secret`;
plugin: `{"plugin", "name", "values"}`, without its secret
settings.

site_id.description: The site to cover. Not together with `customer_id`.

error.description: Why it failed, in plain words; `null` when it went through.

ok.description: Whether the test message went through.

ObjectView.description: One host, cluster, virtual machine or datastore.

details.description:
What it says of itself: for a virtual machine `uuid`, `host`,
`power_state`, `guest_hostname`, `guest_os`, `addresses`, `macs`,
`replication_mode`, `replication_state`; for a host `cluster`,
`connection_state`, `maintenance`, `product`, `vendor`, `model`;
for a datastore `type`.

key.description: Its ID at the source: a managed object ID, or Hyper-V's VM ID.

link_fixed.description: Whether a person decided its server, even none.

matched_by.description:
`uuid`, `mac`, `address`, `name`, or `person` when someone tied
it by hand; `null` without a server.

metrics.description:
Its numbers at the last collection, by measure without the check's
and kind's prefix: `powered_on`, `cpu_usage_ratio`,
`memory_bytes`, `snapshots`, `snapshot_age_seconds`,
`free_ratio`, `alarms_critical`, and so on.

name.description: Its name, as its series' `instance`.

oneOf.description:
For a virtual machine, the server or device it is; `null` when
none is known, or when the viewer cannot read it.

stale.description: Not seen for 15 minutes: the source stopped listing it.

OfflineAlerts.description: Body of the request and of the answer.

OidcSettings.description: An OpenID Connect provider. The client secret is apart.

ca_pem.description:
A certificate authority in PEM to trust besides the public ones, for
a provider with a private certificate.

client_id.description: The client ID the provider gave MonitorFlow.

groups_claim.description: The claim of the ID token, or of userinfo, that lists the groups.

issuer.description:
The provider's issuer, `https`: its discovery document is at
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

scopes.description:
Scopes asked for, separated by spaces; `openid` is required. A
scope the discovery document does not list is left out at sign-in.

OnCallCover.description: A cover: someone on call for a period instead of the rotation.

id.description: The cover's ID, to remove it.

user_id.description: Who is on call during it.

username.description: Name of `user_id`; `null` once the user is removed.

ends_at.description:
After the start, at most 90 days after it; the start within a
year.

user_id.description: Who covers: a member, or someone who could be one.

OnCallGap.description:
Why the person on call cannot be told: a gap. `nobody`: a schedule
without members; `removed`: a removed user's turn; `disabled`;
`no_access`: no longer sees the schedule's place; `no_contact`: no
email address, chat or webhook; `no_mail_server`: only an email
address, and no email channel to send it through.

OnCallMember.description: A member of a schedule, in the order of their turns.

oneOf.description: Why they could not be told now; `null` when they can be.

people.description: By username; disabled users left out.

OnCallPerson.description: Someone who can be on call for a place.

has_contact.description: Whether they set an email address or a chat.

OnCallRotation.description: How often the rotation hands off.

OnCallSchedule.description: A schedule as the screen shows it.

can_manage.description: Whether the caller may change it; always true through an API key.

customer_id.description:
The customer it covers, or the customer of its site; `null` for
everything.

fallback.description:
Who is told during a gap; empty when nobody can be, and for members
who do not manage it.

handoff_day.description: ISO weekday of a weekly hand-off, 1 for Monday; `null` when daily.

mail_host.description:
The mail server personal email goes through; `null` when there is
none, and for members who do not manage it.

members.description: In the order of their turns.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters.

oneOf.description:
The next one who takes over; `null` when nobody else does within
the horizon.
Who is on call now; `null` only without members.

overrides.description: Covers not over yet, by start.

site_id.description: The site it covers; `null` for a whole customer or everything.

time_zone.description: IANA name of the time zone of hand-offs, like `Europe/Paris`.

turns.description:
The turns that start within the next 28 days, the one running
now first.

OnCallScheduleRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/on-call/schedules` and of `PUT` on one.

customer_id.description: The customer it is for; with `site_id` also `null`, everything.

handoff_day.description: ISO weekday, 1 for Monday; needed when weekly.

members.description:
User IDs in order of their turns: 1 to 50, each once, people who
see all of the place (see `GET /api/v1/on-call/people`); members
already on it may stay.

name.description: 1 to 80 characters, trimmed.

site_id.description: The site it is for. Not together with `customer_id`.

OnCallTurn.description: One period with one person on call.

ends_at.description: End of the period, at a hand-off or an end of a cover.

override_id.description: Set when a cover puts this person on.

oneOf.description:
Why this person cannot be told: the period is a gap. `null` when
they can be.

starts_at.description: Start of the period; in the past for the turn running now.

user_id.description: `null` for a removed user's turn or a schedule without members.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

reboot_required.description:
Whether the system waits for a restart; `null` until the agent sent
a report.

reported_at.description: When the agent collected the report, by its clock.

arch.description: Like `amd64` or `x86_64`; `""` when the system has none.

name.description: The package name, or a Windows update's KB number or ID.

reboot_required.description:
A Windows update that may need a restart (pending) or waits for one
(installed); always false for Linux packages.

severity.description:
Like `Critical`; Windows updates only, `null` when Microsoft gives
none.

size_bytes.description: Download size in bytes; Windows updates only.

title.description: Windows updates only (ADR-0049), `null` for Linux packages.

Panel.description: One panel. Fields that do not apply to its kind must be absent.

oneOf.description: Charts and figures.

count.description: Rows of a top list or alerts panel, 1 to 20.

id.description:
Unique within the dashboard, chosen by the client: 1 to 36
letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

instance.description: Only this instance (a disk, a core); every one when absent.

oneOf.description: Top lists.

servers.description: Every server of the dashboard when absent.

width.description: Columns of the three-column grid, 1 to 3; 1 when absent.

PanelCombine.description:
How the servers' series become what a chart or figure shows: `each`
(one line per series, the 8 worst; charts only), `avg`, `max`, `min`,
`sum`, or `count` of servers reporting it (figures only).

servers.description: Servers the panel covers for this viewer.

unavailable.description:
Servers the panel names that are removed or not visible to the
viewer, without saying which.

PanelKind.description:
`chart`: lines over the range. `figure`: one number now. `top`: the
highest or lowest servers now. `alerts`: open incidents.

PanelOrder.description: The order of a top list.

unreachable.description:
Its servers behind a parent that is down (ADR-0152): they open
no incident of their own meanwhile.

oneOf.description: A sentence for the panel; other panels still show.

PanelResult.description: What a panel shows, by its `kind`.

oneOf.description: Every server of the dashboard.
Chosen servers.

PanelServers.description: Which servers a panel shows, within the dashboard's sharing.

PendingHost.description: A host enrolled by a key that asks for approval.

peer_id.description: The ID it was given, which approving or rejecting it takes.

source.description: The IP address it enrolled from; `null` when unknown.

One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

alert_incident_id.description: The alert that started the remediation, if it still exists.

Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a

diagnosis.description: The AI's text: untrusted, shown as data.

incident_id.description: The AI remediation incident it belongs to.

proposed_at.description: When the AI proposed this command.

reason.description: Why the rule gave this tier, in plain words.

reasoning.description: Why the AI proposes this command; untrusted, shown as data.

rule.description:
The rule that gave the tier: `{"source": "builtin" | "configured",
"id"}`.

shell.description:
What runs the command: `posix` (`/bin/sh`) or `powershell`

shell_acceptance.description:
What the server's agent last said it does with these commands:
`accepted`, `off`, `unsupported`, or `null` when unknown (ADR-0076).

snapshots.description:
Whether a change on this server is snapshotted first, on Proxmox
(ADR-0044) or locally (ADR-0094); when not, rollback is limited.

PluginFile.description: A plugin file as `monitorflow-plugin pack` writes it, at most 3 MiB.

MonitorFlow, or the trusted publisher's name; empty for a key not

Hex; `POST /api/plugins` takes it back so what is installed is what

Fingerprints of the catalogue keys built in; none until the

help.description: A sentence under the field; absent without one.

The kind of a setting's field: `secret` values are never shown again

drops.description: Capabilities it no longer asks for.

PluginView.description: A plugin as Administration › Plugins shows it.

enabled.description: Off: no channel sends and no check runs with it.

places.description: Where it may be used; empty: nowhere.

MonitorFlow, the publisher's name, or `null` for a key no longer
trusted.

settings.description: The fields of its settings form.

peak_value.description: The worst judged value while open.

rule.description: The rule as it would be saved.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

points.description:
