silence.

Probe.description: One place a site's checks can run from.

What a new check of a device of this site runs from when it names
none.

`central`, or the relay's name: the instance its checks default

relay_id.description: The relay; `null` for the central server.

probes.description: The central server first, then the relays by name.

local_administrators.description:
Enabled administrators of everything who sign in with a password

redirect_uri.description:
The address to enter as the redirect URI in an OpenID Connect

Whether a client secret or service account password is stored. It

guests.description: By cluster and ID, at most 2000.

When Proxmox last answered whether it can snapshot the guest;

cluster.description: The cluster's name in the central server's configuration.

left_out.description: What a snapshot of the guest does not hold, like a bind mount.

matched_by.description:
Null when mapped by hand, else what discovery matched: `uuid`,

updated_by.description:
Who mapped it by hand; `null` when discovery did, or the account is

cluster.description: A configured cluster that serves the server's customer and site.

node.description: The node's host name: letters, digits and inner `-`.

Guests that match the server equally, when discovery could not

Body of `GET` and `PUT /api/settings/public-address`, and the

address.description: The address in the install commands.

Whether the certificate is issued for `address`; agents refuse to

default.description: The first server name, used when none is chosen.

names.description: The names the server's certificate is issued for.

upstream_url.description:
`upstream_url` and `enroll_url` at `address`, with the published

address.description: A DNS name or IP address; `null` or empty goes back to the default.

query.description: The PromQL the API ran, filters included.

Stable for what it is about, for dismissals: `postgresql`,

A check a recommendation proposes, as the API takes it: a kind and its

A rule MonitorFlow suggests and nobody added or declined yet

key.description: Stable name of the suggestion, like `disk_forecast`.

reason.description:
Sent back to the AI with the rejection, and recorded: 1 to 1000
characters.

cert_not_after.description: Latest expiry among the relay's unrevoked certificates.

connected_agents.description: Agent streams the relay forwards right now.

last_heartbeat.description: Last message on its own stream, live or as last stored.

Seconds the new relay has to connect back before it rolls back, 30
to 3600; 0 or absent for 300.

contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

alert_incident_id.description: The threshold incident that opened it, see `/api/incidents`.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

max_commands.description:
Limits as they were when it opened: commands it may run, and
seconds from `opened_at` before it escalates.

pending_command.description:
The command waiting for approval in `awaiting_approval`, else
`null` (ADR-0043): `id`, `command`, the AI's `diagnosis` and
`reasoning` (untrusted text), the rules' `tier`, `rule` and
`reason`, and `proposed_at`.

chain.description: The hash chain recomputed at this request.

actor_id.description: A user ID, `server`, the AI's provider and model, or a peer ID.

hash.description: SHA-256 of `prev_hash` and this event, hex.

payload.description:
The kind's fields, as recorded. Secrets were redacted before the
event was written; texts from the AI are untrusted.

prev_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous event, hex; zeros for the first one.

seq.description: Position in the incident's chain, from 1.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

low_impact_auto.description: `true`: low-impact commands run without a person's approval.

site_id.description:
The site the row is for; `null` for the customer's row, which
applies to its sites without a row of their own.

updated_by.description: The user who last set it; `null` once that user is deleted.

low_impact_auto.description: `true`: low-impact commands run without a person's approval.

site_id.description:
One of the customer's sites; `null` or absent sets the customer's
own row, which applies to sites without a row of their own.

created_by.description: The user who made it; `null` once that user is deleted.

pattern.description: Normalized: single spaces between words, no trailing `/`.

site_id.description: The site it is narrowed to; `null` for every site of the customer.

rules.description:
By customer, then site (customer-wide rules first), kind and
pattern.

customer_id.description: The customer the rule belongs to.

description.description: Up to 256 characters, no control characters; empty by default.

pattern.description:
For `allow` and `deny`, words where `*` and `?` match within a word
and `**` spans words; an `allow` pattern starts with a program name
without wildcards. For `cache_dir`, an absolute directory of two
components or more, outside system directories. Spaces are
normalized and a trailing `/` dropped before the rule is stored.

site_id.description:
One of the customer's sites to narrow the rule to; `null` or absent
for every site of the customer.

oneOf.description:
`read_only` or `low_impact` for an `allow` rule; `null` or absent
for the other kinds.

channel_recipients.description: The channel's own, used when `recipients` is empty.

last_error.description: Why the last sending failed, in plain words; `null` once one works.

last_period_end.description: The last period sent, and when.

next_from.description: The next report's period and when it goes out.

ReportScheduleRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/report-schedules` and `PUT
/api/report-schedules/{id}`; a change replaces every field.

channel_id.description: An email channel covering the customer, or everything.

csv.description: Attach the CSV; true by default.

customer_id.description: One customer's report; absent or `null` for everything.

enabled.description: True by default; false keeps it without sending.

pdf.description: Attach the PDF; true by default.

recipients.description:
Who gets it, at most 20 addresses; empty or absent for the channel's
own recipients.

time_zone.description:
IANA time zone of the periods and of the times in the report, like
`Europe/Paris`.

error.description: Why not, in plain words; `null` when it went through.

recipients.description: Who it was sent to; empty when it failed.

Retention.description: How long one store keeps data.

applying.description: A change waits for the updater or is being applied.

default_logs.description: Retention of logs when nothing sets it, like `30d`.

default_metrics.description: Retention of metrics when nothing sets it, like `90d`.

error.description: Why the last change failed.

updater_alive.description: A change can be made: the updater runs.

RetentionRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/settings/retention`, in days; `null` leaves a store
alone.

oneOf.description: `unspecified` when absent; recorded in the revocation list.

closed_streams.description: Live streams closed: the peer's and, for a relay, those it forwards.

issued_through.description:
For a relay, the certificates of other peers among `serials`: those
obtained through it (ADR-0028).

serials.description: Certificates put in the CRL, lowercase hexadecimal.

Richer.description:
The fields of a richer threshold (ADR-0153), as the threshold API takes
them; all absent for a plain one.

Role.description: From least to most: `viewer` reads, `operator` also changes, `approver` also approves commands, `administrator` also manages.

RoleGrant.description:
A role granted globally (both IDs null), on one customer and all its
sites (`customer_id`), or on one site (`site_id`). Which sites that
means is resolved by [`super::access::Access`].

customer_id.description: `null` unless granted on a customer.

site_id.description: `null` unless granted on a site.

RoleGrantRequest.description: A role and where it applies; both IDs null is everything.

customer_id.description:
The customer, with all its sites; absent or `null` with `site_id`
for everything.

site_id.description: One site; never with `customer_id`.

local_snapshots.description: MonitorFlow's local snapshots on the host, oldest first.

not_covered.description: System mount points a local snapshot leaves out.

reported_at.description: When the agent last reported its storage.

snapshots.description:
The same object as the approval queue's: `available`, `method`
(`proxmox`, `lvm` or `zfs`), Proxmox's `reason` and `kind`, and
`detail`, a sentence on what a local snapshot covers or why there
is none.

volumes.description: The system volumes from the last report.

Rollup.description:
How each point of a range summarizes the samples since the previous
point. Without it, a point is the last sample before it, so a spike
between two points of a long range is not drawn.

RunningServer.description:
The running server: its version, and the images pinned in `.env`
(`None`: a local build).

SensorConfig.description:
One row of `sensor_configs`. Exactly one of `site_id` and `server_id`
is set.

enabled.description:
`false`: removes the sensor of the same name and instance from the
layers below.

probe.description:
Who runs it (ADR-0148): `null` for the server's agent, `central`
for the central server, `relay` for the relay `probe_relay_id`.

secret_set.description: Whether a website check holds a password, which is never returned.

site_id.description: Set for a site's row, which its servers inherit.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds; `null`: one that grows with the interval.

SensorConfigList.description: Body of the list endpoints, sorted by name and instance.

SensorConfigRequest.description: Body of a create or an update. An update replaces every field.

enabled.description:
`false` removes the sensor of the same name and instance from the
layers below.

instance.description:
What it watches, like a disk or a service: at most 256 bytes
without control characters, `""` by default.

interval_ms.description: How often it runs, in milliseconds: 10000 (10 s) to 86400000 (24 h).

kind.description:
The sensor: `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`, `diskio`, `systemd`, `port`,
`log`, `script`, `eventlog`, `windows_service`, or `plugin` for a
check plugin.

name.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most
64; defaults to `kind`. With `instance`, what a row overrides in the layers
below.

params.description:
The kind's settings: a flat object of strings, numbers and
booleans, at most 32, each value at most 1024 bytes. Unknown
settings are refused.

A website check (`http`, ADR-0150) takes `url` (required),
`method` (`GET` or `HEAD`), `status` (`200-299` by default, like
`200,301-302`), `contains`, `not_contains`, `follow_redirects`
(`true` by default), `headers` (`Name: value` lines), `username`,
`password` and `ip` (`any`, `4` or `6`). `password` is accepted
with an `https://` URL only, kept sealed and never returned: absent
from an update, the stored one is kept; `""` removes it.

probe.description:
Who runs the check, on a server's own row (ADR-0148): `central`
for the central server, or the ID of a relay of the server's site.
Absent or `null`: the server's agent; for a device, which has none,
the relay of its site when there is one, else the central server.
The `instance` of such a check defaults to the probe: `central` or
the relay's name.

timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds it may take, at most `interval_ms`; `null` or absent:
one that grows with the interval.

SensorValue.description: One sensor, by its name and configured instance.

instance.description: `""` when the sensor is not limited to one instance.

metric.description: The metric that stands for it.

reason.description: Why there is no series at all: "No data yet".

series.description: One per instance seen, like one per mount of a disk sensor.

start.description: The sparklines' range and step, in Unix seconds.

SeriesValue.description: One instance of a sensor's metric.

points.description:
`[unix seconds, value]` from `start` to `end`; the value is null
for a step without a sample.

reason.description: Set when the last sample is late: "No data for 5 minutes".

SeriesView.description:
One series: its labels and its `[unix seconds, value]` points. A value
that is not finite is `null`.

labels.description:
`__name__`, `instance`, `peer` (the server's name) and `site`, or
none once aggregated.

oneOf.description:
The last time AI commands were turned on or off from the web
interface, `null` if never (ADR-0098).

The certificate issued last to this agent, revoked or not; `null`
when the CA never issued one (a server row created by hand).

ServerDetail.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/{id}`: the listing row plus the agent's
current certificate.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

servers.description: By site name, hostname and name.

series.description: The series the rule judges, by instance, at most 20.

truncated.description: More series matched than were replayed.

mirror_public_url.description:
Base URL agents reach the package mirror at, written into the
package sources sent to them; a `null` value refuses source
configuration commands.

oneOf.description:
`null` without an updater that reports it, as outside the compose
deployment: the stores' flags are then not this server's to set.

session_idle_timeout.description: A session unused this long ends, in seconds.

session_lifetime.description: Longest session in the web interface, in seconds.

ServerSettingsRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/settings/server`: replaces all three; `null` is the
default.

mirror_public_url.description: An http or https URL without user, query or fragment.

session_idle_timeout.description: Seconds, 300 to 86400, and no longer than the lifetime.

ServerState.description:
The one status of a server on the fleet's pages, worst first
(ADR-0130): a silence wins, then being unreachable behind a parent that
is down (ADR-0152), then being offline, then the worst open
incident nobody acknowledged; a server whose open incidents are all
acknowledged is `acknowledged`, the rest `ok`.

ServerSummary.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/summary`: how many servers are in each
[`ServerState`], out of `total`.

unreachable.description: Behind a parent that is down (ADR-0152).

waiting.description: Made by an import and waiting for their agent (ADR-0146).

version.description: A release version like `0.2.0`, newer than the running one.

id.description: The `update.id` of the update once the updater takes it.

ServerView.description:
One server. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

oneOf.description:
The latest acknowledgement of its open incidents (ADR-0130);
`null` when none is acknowledged.

address.description: A device's address, which its checks reach; `null` for an agent.

agent_version.description: Version reported by the live stream, else the one last stored.

awaiting_agent.description:
Made by an import and waiting for its agent, which takes it over
by enrolling with `peer_id` (ADR-0146).

cert_not_after.description:
Latest expiry among the agent's unrevoked certificates; `null` when
it has none. Past dates mean every certificate has expired.

command_kinds.description:
What its agent last said it does with each command kind: `accepted`,
`off` or `unsupported` (ADR-0076). `null`, or a kind missing here, is
unknown: its agent or a relay on the way does not report yet.

connected_at.description: Start of the current stream, when online.

customer_id.description: Customer of the site (ADR-0026).

hostname.description: The machine's host name, as its agent reports it.

kind.description:
`agent`: the machine runs the agent; `device`: an address without
one, watched by network checks from a probe (ADR-0148).

last_heartbeat.description:
Last message received: from the live stream when online, else the
last time recorded in the database.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether it opens an incident when offline (ADR-0072); muted when
this or `site_offline_alerts` is `false`.

open_incidents.description: Threshold and offline incidents currently open on this server.

os_family.description:
`debian`, `rhel`, `windows`, or `linux` for any other distribution;
`device` for a device.

os_version.description: Like `12` or `9.4`; `null` until the agent reports it.

package_updates.description: Whether the host can take package updates and sources (ADR-0063).

peer_id.description:
The agent's name, given when it was installed; the `peer` label of
its metrics.

relay_id.description: The relay its last connection came through; `null` when direct.

revoked_at.description: When it was removed; `null` while it is in the fleet.

oneOf.description: That silence: who made it and why (ADR-0130); `null` without one.

silenced_until.description: While a silence covers it, when the last one ends (ADR-0079).

state.description: Its one status on the fleet's pages (ADR-0130).

oneOf.description:
While a parent it depends on is down (ADR-0152): which, and its
incident; `null` otherwise.

via_relay.description: Peer ID of the relay carrying the live stream, if any.

cap_bytes.description: At least 1 GiB, in bytes; `null` for the default.

locked.description: The configuration sets it; the page cannot change it.
The configuration sets it; the page cannot change it.

Shell.description: The shell that runs a server's commands, which decides the rules.

SilenceNote.description: Who silenced a server, until when and why (ADR-0130).

by.description: Who made the silence; `null` once the account is removed.

window.description:
An occurrence of a maintenance window (ADR-0151): "In maintenance
until 04:00".

checks.description:
Only these checks of the server, or of every server of the site
(ADR-0151): 1 to 20. Absent or `null`: everything of the target.

ends_at.description: After the start, at most 30 days later.

reason.description: Why, for others: 1 to 200 characters, trimmed.

target_id.description: The server, relay, site or customer; absent for `all`.

can_end.description: Whether this user may end it.

checks.description:
Only these checks of its server or site; `null` for all of it
(ADR-0151).

customer_id.description: The target's customer; `null` for `all`.

ends_at.description: When it ends on its own.

reason.description: Why, as its maker wrote it.

site_id.description: The target's site; `null` for `customer` and `all`.

target_name.description:
The server's hostname, or the relay's, site's or customer's name;
`null` for `all`.

window_id.description:
The maintenance window it is an occurrence of, `null` for a one-off
silence (ADR-0151).

SilencedCheck.description: A check, by its identity in `sensor_configs`.

instance.description: What it watches, `""` (the default) for every instance it writes.

name.description: The check's name, like `service_nginx` or `disk`.

more_servers.description: The site has more servers than were replayed.

servers.description: Up to 20 servers of the site, by name.

SitePreviewServer.description: One server of a site preview.

incidents.description: Incidents the rule would have opened on it, every series together.

SiteSensors.description:
Body of `GET /api/sites/{id}/sensors`: what the site's servers run
unless they override it.

check_interval_ms.description: Interval of the built-in checks, in milliseconds (ADR-0097).

servers.description: Every enrolled server of the site.

SiteSourcesChange.description: Answer of the site's changes: each server is queued or skipped alone.

queued.description: Servers a command was queued for.

skipped.description:
Servers that needed the change but could not take it now. Servers
already as asked are in neither list.

os_family.description: As in the server listing, so Windows rows read differently.

SiteThresholds.description:
Body of `GET /api/sites/{id}/thresholds/effective`: what the site's
servers get unless they override it.

thresholds.description: By metric and instance, muted ones included.

agent_auto_update.description:
The site's automatic update override: `null` follows the
server-wide setting (ADR-0055).

agent_auto_update_effective.description: Whether automatic updates apply to the site, override or not.

name.description: Unique across customers; the `site` label of every metric.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether servers and relays of the site open incidents when offline
(ADR-0072).

relay_count.description: Relays of the site, removed ones left out.

server_count.description: Servers of the site, removed ones left out.

SkippedServer.description: A server a site's change left out, and why.

error.description: Why it failed; `null` otherwise.

mode.description: The mode it was built in: an on-demand snapshot holds indexes only.

name.description: Such as `20261023T090000Z`; servers' sources name it.

SnapshotKept.description:
Why a snapshot stays, the strongest reason when there are several:
it is `current`, a campaign, a server or a relay uses it, or it is among
the newest kept.

name.description:
1 to 64 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `.`, `_` and `-`, not starting with a dot
and not `current`; the UTC time such as `20261023T090000Z` when
absent or `null`.

SnapshotSet.description: The snapshots of one name, taken together.

delete_after.description: When retention deletes it at the latest.

SnapshotState.description: State of a snapshot; only `published` ones are served under their name.

SnapshotSupport.description:
Whether the server can be snapshotted; without it the interface shows
that rollback is limited.

detail.description:
With `cannot_snapshot`: what Proxmox cannot snapshot, like "rootfs
is on storage local (dir), which cannot take snapshots".

oneOf.description: The mapped guest's kind, so the reason can say VM or container.

left_out.description: What a snapshot does not hold, though Proxmox takes one.

oneOf.description:
Why no local snapshot, as a code and its values, for a client to
word in its own language; `detail` says it in English. Absent
unless a local snapshot was looked for and is not possible.

method.description:
Which snapshot a change gets when available: `proxmox`, or a local
`lvm` or `zfs` snapshot (ADR-0094).

oneOf.description: Why it stays.

SnapshotView.description:
A snapshot and why it stays; `null` when the next pass of retention
removes it, or while it is created.

metric.description: The series of its value, and of its state when it has one.

SnmpChannel.description: One channel as stored, with its limits and last values.

SnmpChannelLimits.description: Limits of one channel: an ordinary threshold of the device (ADR-0017).

duration_s.description: Seconds past the limit before an incident opens, 0 by default.

key.description: The metric suffix; from the name when absent.

oneOf.description:
The channel's limits on its value; absent or `null` for none. A
channel with a lookup or an expected text also alerts on its state.

match.description:
For a text: `contains`, `not_contains`, `equals`, `not_equals`,
`matches` or `not_matches`, with `expect` and `severity`.

name.description: What people read: "Sessions".

oid.description: A numeric OID: an object (`...8.0`), or a column of `table`.

SnmpChannelSuggestion.description: What a channel reading an object should be.

lookup.description: A built-in lookup, when one fits.

table.description: For a column: its table and the column naming the rows.

SnmpChannelValue.description: One value a channel wrote, by row.

instance.description: The table's row; `""` for one object.

state.description: 0 OK, 1 warning, 2 critical, for a text or a lookup.

text.description: The value's name or the text.

SnmpCheck.description: One custom check of a device.

name.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, like `snmp_fw`; a change keeps
the name of the path.

probe.description: `central` or a relay of the site; absent: the site's default.

table.description:
For a table: its OID (the table or its entry), and the column whose
values name the rows.

SnmpCredentials.description: What the API shows of a device's credentials: never a secret.

community_set.description: Whether a community is stored, for v1 and v2c.

SnmpCredentialsRequest.description:
Body of the credentials of a device: `version` and what it needs. On a
change, a secret left out keeps the stored one when the version stays.

auth_protocol.description:
v3: `sha`, `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512` or `md5`; absent for no
authentication.

community.description: v1 and v2c: the community. Secret.

priv_protocol.description:
v3: `aes128`, `aes256` or `aes256c` (Cisco's key extension); absent
for no privacy. Needs authentication.

SnmpLookup.description: One lookup: built in, or a customer's own.

can_change.description: Whether this user may change or remove it.

customer_id.description: `null` for a built-in lookup.

otherwise.description: The state of a value no entry names: `ok`, `warning` or `critical`.

lookups.description: The built-in ones first, then by name.

customer_id.description: May be left out when there is only one customer; a change keeps it.

entries.description:
1 to 100 entries, each `{"value": 1, "name": "OK", "state": "ok"}`,
a range `{"value": 10, "max": 19, ...}` or a text `{"text": "on", ...}`.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, unique per customer.
Its file name, for the list and errors.

text.description: The file's text, at most 1 MiB.

files.description: 1 to 20 files; modules that import one another may come together.

SnmpMibUploaded.description:
What an upload added: each module, and the enumerations it offers as
lookups.

offered_lookups.description:
For "Make a lookup": the objects with named values, with the states
their names suggest.

module.description: The MIB module, or the vendor for the library.

names.description:
For `oids`: the OID asked, then the name with the instance, like
`ifInOctets.3`.

objects.description:
For `q`: at most 200, the library first. For `oids`: one per OID
named, keyed by the OID asked.

name.description: The object or type it comes from, like `raidStatus`.

SnmpRead.description: Body of the answer of a read.

name.description: What a MIB or the library calls it, like `ifInOctets.3`.

type.description:
`Integer`, `OctetString`, `Counter64`, `TimeTicks`..., or
`noSuchObject` when the device has none.

value.description: The value as text: printable text, or hexadecimal bytes.

max.description: For a walk: 500 objects by default, 2000 at most.

probe.description: `central` or a relay of the site; absent: the site's default.

walk.description: Or an OID whose subtree to walk ("Browse").

SnmpTemplate.description: A kind of device: its groups and thresholds.

rows.description: At most 50 rows for a table.

SnmpTestedChannel.description: One channel of one row in a test.

note.description:
In words, when there is nothing to write: "A rate comes from the
next reading", "No such object".

type.description: The SNMP type and raw value read, or why none.

value.description: What the channel would write: its value, state and text.

instance.description: The table's row; `""` for one object.

SourceView.description: Whether a source was read at its last collection.

error.description: The message, in English, such as what to do about it.

reason.description:
Why not: `connect`, `tls`, `certificate`, `login`, `api` for a
vCenter; `not_installed`, `denied`, `failed` for Hyper-V.

SourcesMode.description:
`replace` sets the host's other sources aside, `add` keeps them
(ADR-0032).

add_mirror.description: The fix is adding [`Self::distribution`] on the Mirrors page.

campaign.description: A campaign has the sources for now.

oneOf.description: A change on its way to the server; `null` when none.

distribution.description:
The catalog's name for what the server runs, such as `Debian 12`;
`null` when no mirror matches it.

failed.description: Why the last change failed, when none succeeded or started since.

mirrors.description: With `mirror`: the mirrors and snapshots used. Empty otherwise.

problem.description:
Why the server cannot use a mirror, in a sentence for the page;
`null` when it can.

problem_code.description:
[`Self::problem`] as a code, for a client to word in its own
language: `no_package_updates`, `windows`, `no_distribution`,
`no_catalog`, `not_enabled`, `no_mirror` or `copying`. Its values
are [`Self::distribution`] and the server's OS version.

using.description: What the last change that succeeded left; `own` when none did.

oneOf.description:
Windows servers: where Windows Update takes updates from, from the
latest package report. `null` on Linux and until an agent that
reports it sends a report (ADR-0086).

SourcesUsing.description: Where a server's packages come from.

locked.description: `.env` sets it by hand, which wins over the web interface.

value.description: The value of its `-retentionPeriod` flag, like `90d`.

invalid.description: Overflowed, so it can no longer be rolled back to.

name.description: The set's name, shared by its volumes.

origin.description: `vg/lv` or the dataset it is a snapshot of.

size_bytes.description: Space it holds: the classic LVM snapshot's size, ZFS's `used`.

source.description: `vg/lv` of the snapshot for LVM, `dataset@name` for ZFS.

used_percent.description:
Classic LVM only: how full the snapshot is, in percent; at 100 it
is invalid.

free_bytes.description:
What snapshots draw from: the volume group's free space for classic
LVM, the thin pool's for thin LVM, the dataset's available space
for ZFS.

metadata_percent.description: Thin pools only: how full the pool's metadata is, in percent.

pool_bytes.description:
The size of that space: the volume group, the thin pool, or the
dataset's used plus available space.

source.description: `vg/lv` for LVM, the dataset for ZFS, the device otherwise.

by_roots.description: Whether the probe's roots trust it without a fingerprint.

fingerprint.description:
`AB:CD:…`, to compare with the one the vCenter shows and send back
as `fingerprint`.

not_after.description: When it expires; `null` when it does not read.

trusted.description:
Whether it is trusted: by the probe's roots, or by the fingerprint
given.

managers.description:
Every third-party manager of the server's platform, present or
not, by name.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

packages.description: Apps by manager, ID and scope.

reported.description:
False until the agent reports third-party managers: an agent or
relay before ADR-0138. `managers` and `packages` are then empty.

api_key.description: An API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. It acts as its maker, narrowed to its reach, access and areas.

tags.name: servers
tags.description: The servers MonitorFlow watches: one machine each, with its agent. Lists and details carry the live connection status, open incidents, silences and certificate expiry. Area `servers`; any key may list servers within its reach.

tags.name: sites
tags.description: Sites group servers and relays, usually one per place or network; customers own sites. A single company has one customer. Sites and customers are listed by any key within its reach; creating them is in the `administration` area.

tags.name: alerts
tags.description: Incidents are opened and resolved by MonitorFlow when a threshold is crossed or a server stops reporting; the API reads and acknowledges them. Silences stop notifications about a server, relay, site, customer or everything for a while. Area `alerts`.

tags.name: updates
tags.description: Commands sent to a server's agent: package updates and agent updates, queued, sent as soon as the agent is connected, with their output. Area `updates`.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: Commands the AI proposed to fix an incident that the rules held for a person: approve, edit or reject them. The AI's text is untrusted and shown as data. Area `remediation`.

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Values a server's sensors reported, now or over a range. You name a server, a metric and optionally an instance; MonitorFlow builds the query itself and never accepts raw PromQL. Area `servers`.

tags.name: servers
tags.description: Servers, sites and customers

tags.name: alerts
tags.description: Incidents, silences and maintenance windows

tags.name: updates
tags.description: Commands sent to servers

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: What the AI did about alerts. Each remediation incident is one alert the AI worked on, with every step recorded in a hash chain: the context it was sent after redaction, its proposals, how the rules classified each command, who approved or rejected it, and what the agent ran and printed. Read-only, except the approval queue, where people decide the commands the rules parked for them. The AI's text is untrusted: show it as data. Needs the key area "remediation".

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Metric queries built by MonitorFlow, never raw PromQL

tags.name: health
tags.description: Probes for load balancers and monitoring: whether the central server's process serves requests and whether its database answers. They need no key and say nothing beyond up or down.

tags.name: server-update
tags.description: Updates of the central server itself, carried out by the updater service of the compose deployment: what runs, whether a newer signed release exists, and the request that installs one. The updater takes a backup first and rolls back by itself when the new version does not start. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "updates" area.

tags.name: backups
tags.description: Backups of the whole central server, taken by the updater: once a day, before each update and on request; the 7 latest are kept. A backup holds the database of every customer and the server's keys, including the certificate authority's, so only a global administrator lists, takes or downloads them; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. Every download is in the audit log.

tags.name: certificate-authority
tags.description: The certificate authority that signs the certificates of the central server, relays and agents for mTLS. These operations show when it expires and change it, planned or after a suspected compromise; they never hand out a key or a certificate. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area.

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Settings of the whole central server: where install commands download the agent, the address hosts reach the server at, AI, session lifetimes, the package mirror's address, how long metrics and logs are kept, and automatic agent updates. Values the server's configuration file sets win: they are shown as locked and a request to change them is refused with 409. Every change is in the audit log with the old and new values. Changes are a global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer" and reach "Everything", in the "administration" area, except automatic updates, in the "updates" area.

tags.name: users
tags.description: The accounts of people who sign in to the web interface, and the roles they hold: viewer, operator, approver or administrator, on everything, one customer or one site. Only a global administrator manages them; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. A key can grant any role, administrator of everything included, to an existing account, as its maker can. Inviting a user and issuing a password link hand out a credential for a person, so they are left out of the public API and done in the web interface. No change may leave the server without an active administrator of everything, and nobody may disable or remove their own account. Every change is in the audit log.

tags.name: license
tags.description: The subscription's license key: its tier (Basic, Standard, Premium or Enterprise), the managed and central servers it covers and its dates, checked offline. Without one the install is on the free Community tier, with every feature. A valid key moves the central server to the tested update channel; an Enterprise key allows additional central servers on one database. A global administrator's; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area.

tags.name: sign-in
tags.description: Sign-in providers: OpenID Connect providers (Entra ID, Google, Okta, Keycloak, authentik and any other that follows the standard) and LDAP directories over LDAPS or StartTLS only. People sign in through them with the provider's own password and second factor; their account is made at their first sign-in, and its roles are those its groups give under "Groups and roles", replaced at each sign-in and as soon as the groups change. Someone in no mapped group cannot sign in. One administrator of everything with a password kept by MonitorFlow always remains, so a provider that is down never locks everyone out. A provider is turned on only once its connection test passes. Secrets are stored encrypted and never returned. Only a global administrator manages these; with a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. Every change is in the audit log. Signing in itself is done in a browser and is not part of this API.

tags.name: dashboards
tags.description:
Pages of panels (charts, figures, top lists and open alerts) kept for one person ("Only me") or shared with a site or a customer. Viewers of a site or customer see its dashboards; any role above viewer makes, changes and deletes them; anyone who can read makes their own. With a key, the "dashboards" area; a key sees, changes and deletes its maker's "Only me" dashboards whatever its reach, but the data of any panel is only ever read within the key's reach. A panel never shows more than the person asking may read: its servers are resolved again on every read, and servers they cannot see are counted, not named.

Display links, which show dashboards on a wall screen without signing in, are made, listed and turned off only in the web interface, by an administrator of the dashboards' site or customer (or of anything for their own). A link's secret is in the URL fragment, shown once; a screen trades it for a session of one hour. Whoever holds the URL sees the link's dashboards, up to 12, and nothing else: no other page, no settings, no change. Each screen request reads as the link's maker with their roles of the moment, so a maker who is disabled or loses the role stops their links. A link may expire or never; deleting a dashboard removes it from its links. Because a link reads with all its maker's roles and outlives a key, `/api/v1/display-links`, `/api/v1/dashboards/{id}/display-links` and `/api/v1/display` answer 404.

tags.name: plugins
tags.description: Signed WebAssembly plugins that add checks, run by agents, and notification channels, run by the central server, in a sandbox that reaches only the hosts its manifest names. Installing, updating, placing, turning off and removing plugins, and trusting the publisher keys that sign them, are a global administrator's: a plugin runs on the central server or on the agents it is given to. With a key, access "Administer", reach "Everything" and the "administration" area. Which plugins may be used where is read by anyone who can read, limited to the places they see. Every change is in the audit log.

tags.name: sensors
tags.description: What each server checks and how often. A server runs the built-in checks (cpu, memory, disk and disk activity, every minute or at its site's interval), overlaid with its site's rows, then its own: a row replaces the sensor of the same name and instance below it, and a disabled row removes it. Agents pick up a change within seconds; the effective view says whether the agent runs the current configuration. Offline alerts and the site's check interval are here too. Area `alerts`.

tags.name: thresholds
tags.description: When a metric opens an incident. Every server is checked against the built-in thresholds (CPU, memory, disk space, disk wait), overlaid with its site's rows, then its own: a row replaces the threshold of the same metric and instance below it, and a disabled row turns it off. A threshold opens a warning or critical incident once the value has stayed past it for `duration_s`, and resolves it once the value is back by more than the recovery margin (`hysteresis`). Area `alerts`.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: Notification channels: where messages to people go when an incident opens, gets worse or ends, a command waits for approval, an update fails, a backup fails or a new version is out. A channel is an email address list sent through a mail server, a webhook, a chat channel (`slack`, `teams`, `discord`) or a plugin's, and notifies about everything, one customer or one site. Only administrators reach channels, and only those of what they administer: everything takes a global administrator (a key with every reach), a customer an administrator of it, a site an administrator of it or of its customer; others answer 404. Secrets are write-only: the mail password, signing secret, chat webhook URL or plugin secret settings go in `secret` and never come back, a channel says only `has_secret`, and a webhook shows only its URL's origin, as its path and query often hold a token. A channel saved by anyone but a global administrator only sends to public addresses. Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `alerts` area. For machines rather than people, use an integration.

tags.name: integrations
tags.description: Integrations: another tool, like a PSA or an automation, that gets MonitorFlow's events as one signed JSON `POST` per event: incidents, servers, updates, campaigns and approvals, each integration choosing which. The body follows [`docs/events/v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Kidoly/monitorflow/blob/main/docs/events/v1.schema.json); the receiver's rules and code to check signatures are in [`docs/integrations.md`](https://github.com/Kidoly/monitorflow/blob/main/docs/integrations.md). In short: each request carries `X-MonitorFlow-Event`, `X-MonitorFlow-Delivery` (the event's `id`), `X-MonitorFlow-Timestamp` and `X-MonitorFlow-Signature`, `sha256=` and the HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{raw body}` under the integration's signing secret, plus `X-MonitorFlow-Replay: 1` when sent again. Delivery is at least once: de-duplicate on the `id`. Anything but a 2xx within 15 seconds is retried after 30 seconds, then twice as long each time up to an hour, for 24 hours; an integration that accepts nothing for 24 hours is turned off and administrators are told. Events are kept 30 days and can be sent again with the same IDs. An integration notifies about everything, one customer or one site, and is managed by the administrators of that place, like a notification channel; others get 404. The URL and the signing secret are write-only: answers show the URL's origin, as its path and query often hold a token, and the secret only once, when it is made. Private and local addresses need a global administrator (a key with every reach). Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `administration` area.

tags.name: on-call
tags.description: On call: who is told of each alert of a place in person, besides the channels, in turns. A schedule is for everything, one customer or one site; its members take turns, handing off every day or every week at a local time in its time zone, and a cover puts someone else on call for a period. A gap is a period when the person on call cannot be told (no contact, disabled, removed, no longer sees the place); the nearest administrators are told instead. Schedules are managed by the administrators of their place, like notification channels: everything takes a global administrator (a key with every reach), a customer an administrator of it, a site an administrator of it or of its customer; others get 404. Only people who see all of the place can be put on a schedule. How each person is reached is theirs to set and not in the public API. Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `alerts` area.

tags.name: follow-up
tags.description: Follow-up: who is told next when nobody acknowledges a critical incident, step after step, for everything, one customer or one site. A step waits a number of minutes without acknowledgement, then tells the person on call of schedules, named people, notification channels or the nearest administrators. Where no follow-up is set, the default applies: the nearest administrators, after 15 minutes, once. The most precise follow-up of an incident's place applies: its site's, else its customer's, else everything's. An incident shows where it is in its follow-up (`GET /api/v1/incidents/{id}`), and acknowledging it stops the follow-up. Follow-ups are managed by the administrators of their place, like notification channels; others get 404, or 403 when saving. Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `alerts` area.

tags.name: enrollment
tags.description: Bringing servers and relays into MonitorFlow. An enrollment token is single-use: it enrolls one named server or relay on one site within its validity (one hour by default). An install key is reusable: it enrolls any number of servers (or one relay) on one site for up to a year, names each after its host, and can make new hosts wait for an administrator's approval. Both are secrets shown once, in the answer that creates them; no route returns them again and an `Idempotency-Key` replay does not either. Every route needs the administrator role on the site's customer, given globally or for that customer: a site's administrator cannot enroll. Through an API key, that means access "Administer", the "administration" area, and a reach of everything or of the customer.

tags.name: relays
tags.description: Relays: one per site where servers cannot reach the central server, or should not each open a connection to it. A relay forwards its site's agents to the central server, can serve package mirrors and releases on its network, and is enrolled like a server. Reading relays needs any role on their site; removing, updating and confirming the names of one needs the administrator role on its customer. Through an API key, relays are in the "servers" area, their updates in "updates"; listing them is open to any key within its reach.

tags.name: agent releases
tags.description: The MonitorFlow releases this server holds and serves to install commands and to agent and relay updates, so that servers without Internet access can install and update. Every release is checked against the release keys built into the server before it is kept. Importing one is for global administrators, since every customer uses the same releases.

tags.name: mirrors
tags.description: Package mirrors: copies of the apt and dnf repositories of the distributions servers run, kept on this server and on relays, so servers update without reaching the Internet and every server of a campaign installs the same packages. A mirror syncs on a schedule; a snapshot freezes what a sync copied under a name and never changes, and `current` is the newest one. Mirrors are shared by every customer, so every route is for global administrators: through an API key, access "Administer", reach everything and the "updates" area.

tags.name: package sources
tags.description: Where a server's apt or dnf takes its packages from: its own sources or the mirrors of this install. Changing them sends the server a signed `configure_sources` or `revert_sources` command, which the agent applies and can undo. Reading them needs any role on the server's site; changing them needs the administrator role on its customer. Through an API key, these routes are in the "updates" area. Windows servers have no mirror: their status says where Windows Update takes their updates from instead.

tags.name: risk rules
tags.description: How MonitorFlow decides what an AI command may do. Every command the AI proposes is classified by rules, never by the AI: `read_only` runs at once, `low_impact` waits for a person with an approver role unless the site's policy lets it run on its own, `high_impact` waits for an administrator, and `forbidden` never runs and hands the incident to a person. Built-in rules cover the commands MonitorFlow knows; administrators add allow rules for other commands (read-only or low impact only), deny patterns that forbid commands, and cache directories that may be cleared, for a customer or one of its sites. Rules and policies need a role on the customer as a whole (everything, or the customer): a role on one site, or a key that reaches one site, sees none. They need the key area "remediation".

tags.name: campaigns
tags.description: Package or agent updates sent to many servers of one customer, in batches (`waves`), inside maintenance windows, stopping when a batch fails more than its failure threshold. Targets are frozen when the campaign is made; nothing is sent before it is started. Every server gets a signed command of its own, `apply_updates` (or `self_update` for an agent update campaign), queued behind any other command of that server and checked by its agent, which runs package updates only when its administrator allowed them. Campaign commands are made by an administrator, not the AI: the risk rules and the approval queue do not apply to them. Reading needs a role on the customer as a whole (everything or the customer); creating and acting need an administrator role on it. Needs the key area "updates".

tags.name: automatic updates
tags.description: Agents and relays update themselves to the newest stable release the central server holds, never newer than the server: per site, one server first, then a quarter of the site at a time, never the host's packages and never a restart of the host. A rollout halts everywhere after too many failures until a global administrator resumes it. These routes need a global administrator and the key area "updates"; the settings themselves are under `/settings/auto-update`.

tags.name: imports
tags.description: Moving from another monitoring tool. An import reads the other tool's configuration, from export files or through its API, and shows first what MonitorFlow would create: servers waiting for their agent, checks, thresholds, silences (of servers or of chosen checks), maintenance windows that come back (ADR-0151) and notification channels. Windows whose source does not say its time zone, like Zabbix's and PRTG's, are read in the request's `time_zone`. Each item is in one of three lists: `exact` (MonitorFlow does the same), `approximated` (close, the note says how it differs) or `not_movable` (the note says why), and says whether MonitorFlow has it already (`present`). Nothing is created until the preview is confirmed, with the items to leave out; items that need one left out are left out too. Importing the same configuration again creates nothing twice. An import can be undone: what it created goes, except servers an agent has taken over. Servers then only need the agent: one that enrolls with a server's ID, or with an install key of its site from a host of that name, takes it over with its checks. The other tool is only read, never changed, and can keep running. A connection's token is used for the request and never stored. Administrators of the target site only; everything is in the audit log. API keys need the `administration` area.

tags.name: devices
tags.description: Devices: switches, routers, printers, UPSs or any address watched without the agent, by network checks that run from the central server or from a relay of the device's site (a probe). A device is a server of kind `device`: it is listed, read, silenced, charted and removed with the server routes, its checks are `sensor_configs` rows with a `probe`, and its thresholds are a server's. It is never offline nor waiting for an agent: its checks say what is wrong. The same probe checks can watch a server that has the agent, from outside. Operators of the site add and change devices. Area `servers`.

tags.name: network-scans
tags.description: Network scans: a range of a site's IP addresses tried from the central server or a relay of the site (ping, a few TCP ports, SNMP with the credentials the site's devices have and those given to the scan, the MAC address on the probe's own link, the name from reverse DNS), at most 50 probes a second and never outside the range. Each run keeps what answered; the results propose for each address: install the agent (SSH or RDP open), an SNMP device with its template, or a device with its ping and ports, and recognise what the site monitors already. Nothing is added until `POST /api/v1/network-scans/{id}/add`. A scan can run every hour, day or week and say what is new or gone, with an optional notification. Viewers of the site read scans; operators of the site change them. Area `servers`.

tags.name: virtualization
tags.description: VMware and Hyper-V: the hosts, clusters, virtual machines and datastores of a vCenter or ESXi host (a device with a `vmware` check, run from a probe) or of a Hyper-V host (a Windows server with a `hyperv` check), kept from what their checks last reported. Each virtual machine is matched to the server or device of the same customer it is, by its hardware ID, a network card, an address or its name. Area `servers`.

tags.name: snmp
tags.description: What custom SNMP checks of devices read (ADR-0157): lookups that name the values of an enumerated object and give each a state (`ok`, `warning`, `critical`), built in or a customer's own; MIB files a customer uploads to name the objects of its devices; and the names the library of common vendor objects and those MIBs give to OIDs. Lookups and MIBs belong to a customer: anyone who reads one of its sites reads them, and operators and above of the whole customer change them. Custom checks of a device, with their channels and limits, and Test and Browse from the device's probe, are under `/api/v1/devices/{id}/snmp-checks` and `/api/v1/devices/{id}/snmp`. Area `servers`.
